field this slice writes is not yet answered from the tables, and for the one line that lists this
slice's registration function. That is about eight code files in two packages. Nothing under `web/` is
edited: the interface already sends these writes, and the stand-in is read as the statement of the
behaviour, not changed. No migration is added. The size is argued by the count of writes (eight) and by
the golden files each one owes; the difficulty is `reasoning` and not `critical` because no amount shown
or summed changes with this slice, and the default line, the one value here that later moves money, is
stored through the line lookup delivered earlier and acts only through rules that write a visible
history step.

title: Show a card's unknown closing date and next-bill amount as unknown
description:
## What changes for the user
The card page says when the bill closes, the best day to buy, and how much of this month's spending falls on the next bill. For a card whose bank has no known closing rule the app cannot work those out, and today it answers them as blanks and as `R$ 0,00`. A zero there reads as "nothing to set aside", which is not what is known. After this lands such a card shows a dash for each of them.

## Outcome
The card overview closing date, due date, best purchase day and next-bill amount can be unknown in the contract, the backend answers them as unknown for a card with no closing rule, and the card page and the home summary show a dash.

## Context
finwise's interface reaches its backend through a TypeScript contract (`web/src/api/contract/`), described for Go by a generated manifest that the gate keeps current (`npm --prefix web run contract`). The convention, stated in `AGENTS.md`: a field the ledger cannot always answer is nullable in the contract and a screen shows its absence, a dash for an unknown figure; a zero is for a figure that is truly zero.

The Go backend predicts a card's closing date from a table that depends on the bank (`internal/cardrules`). Only one bank has a table. For a card of any other bank the rules answer "unknown" for the closing date and for the amount that falls on the next bill. The contract's `CardOverview` cannot carry that: `closesOn` and `bestPurchaseDay` are required strings and `payAhead.amount` is a required number, so the handler in `internal/api/card.go` writes empty strings and 0. The card in use today belongs to the bank that has a table, so the case does not show on screen yet; it will the day the card in use is another bank's.

The home summary's pay-ahead is already nullable and is offered only when known.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In the contract, `CardOverview.closesOn`, `CardOverview.dueOn`, `CardOverview.bestPurchaseDay` and the pay-ahead amount of the card overview are nullable, and the manifest is regenerated.
- [ ] Over a fixture card of a bank with no closing table, `card.overview` answers `null` for the four, and still answers its limit and its past bills. The due date of the open bill is unknown when the open bill cannot be placed, so it is not guessed from an older bill.
- [ ] The card page shows a dash for each of the four and no "R$ 0,00" for the next-bill amount; a test mounts it over the stand-in with such a card.
- [ ] Over the prototype dataset nothing changes: `npm --prefix web run parity` still reports every state at or under 0.05%.
- [ ] The backend's golden files for the card are re-recorded from the fixture ledgers and its answers still validate against the schema.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, parity is unchanged, and a card with no closing table shows four dashes.

## Tests
- Unit: the handler over a card with no table.
- Component: the card page over the stand-in with unknown closing fields.
- Conformance: the stand-in's and the backend's card answers against the regenerated schema.
- Golden: the card overview's answers.
- Parity: the full run, unchanged.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/api/contract/card.ts`, `web/src/screens/contas/CardScreen.vue`, `web/src/api/fake/card-rules.ts`, `web/src/test/`, `internal/contract/contract.json`, `internal/api/card.go`, `internal/api/card_test.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/`
**Reads only:** `internal/cardrules/`, `web/src/lib/format.ts`, `AGENTS.md`, `bin/ci`

Three fields of one contract type become nullable, one screen and one handler follow, and the generated manifest and the card's golden files are refreshed.
close_reason: CardOverview.closesOn, dueOn, bestPurchaseDay and the pay-ahead amount are nullable in the contract and the manifest is regenerated. For a card of a bank with no closing table the handler answers null for the four and still answers the limit and the past bills; the stand-in answers the same; the card page shows a dash for each and no formatted zero. The monthly closing shows no card bill when the next-bill amount is unknown. bin/ci: CI green on the tree merged with main, 887 tests. Parity: 174 checked, 0 over 0.05%. No fixture ledger holds such a card, so the case is covered by unit tests and schema conformance and has no golden file.

title: Make every screen hold on a fresh install
description:
## What changes for the user
Every screen was built against a design that shows a year of use: a budget, subscriptions, months already closed, a chart with history. Nobody has seen the app on its first day, and a real backend that only reads the bank's records is exactly that first day. Today several screens would show `NaN`, a blank area or nothing at all. After this lands every screen opens cleanly both when the bank data exists and nothing else does, and when there is no data whatsoever: zero where zero is true, a dash where a figure is not known, a short sentence where a list is empty.

## Outcome
The in-memory stand-in can start in two new states, a fresh install with bank data and an empty ledger; the contract is nullable wherever a fresh install has no honest value; every screen renders both states without an error; and a test sweeps every route over both.

## Context
finwise's interface (`web/`, Vue 3) reaches its backend through a TypeScript contract, `FinwiseApi` (`web/src/api/types.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/`). An in-memory stand-in (`web/src/api/fake/`) implements it over the design prototype's dataset, and `createFakeApi(options)` accepts a `state`. A real, read-only backend is being built: it will answer what the bank's records support and return everything the person authors inside the app (budget, budget lines on transactions, tags, nicknames, subscriptions, review marks, settings) as on a fresh install. The design prototype has no first-run screens, so those states were never built or measured.

A generated manifest, `internal/contract/contract.json`, carries a JSON Schema for every method's result, and an existing test validates the stand-in's answers against it. Changing a contract type means regenerating the manifest (the gate fails otherwise).

**Two states.**
- *Fresh install*: accounts, transactions, the card's bills, pots and investments exist; nothing the person authors does. Transactions have no budget line, no tag, no nickname and nobody classified them; pots have no bucket, no target and no linked line; there is no budget, no subscription, nothing to review, no closed month; settings are the defaults.
- *Empty ledger*: nothing at all, as before the first synchronisation. No account, no transaction, no card, no pot.

Both are built from invented data, like every fixture in the repository.

**Never invent a value.** Where the contract requires a field that has no honest value in one of these states, the field becomes nullable in the contract and the screen learns to show its absence. Known candidates, to be confirmed against the types: who classified a transaction when it has no line; the bucket of a pot and of an account; the card overview when there is no card; the last backup in the settings; the suggested threshold with no corrections behind it; the salary account's balance with no such account. A zero is used only where zero is the truth (a budget cap with no budget is 0). The full list of widened fields goes in the pull request.

**What the screens show.** Follow the vocabulary the interface already has: the empty block of the transaction list (`web/src/components/transactions/TransactionList.vue`) for an empty list, a dash for an unknown figure, `R$ 0,00` for a true zero. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese. No new visual component and no new token unless a state cannot be expressed without one; a color, size, radius, shadow or spacing step is never written as a literal.

**Known breaks.** `web/src/screens/patrimonio/chartGeometry.ts` divides by the chart's maximum with no guard for zero. `FakeState.card` is required, so a state with no card does not type-check. The Início, Budget, Patrimônio and card screens were partly read and assume their objects exist; Revisão, Cofrinhos, Assinaturas, Contas, Configuração and the transaction panel were not audited at all.

**The design does not move.** The prototype's dataset and every existing parity state stay as they are: the parity check must report the same result. The new states have no reference to be measured against, so they are covered by tests and looked at by a person.

**Looking at it.** The dev server starts the stand-in in one of the new states when `VITE_FINWISE_STATE` is `fresh` or `empty` (`VITE_FINWISE_STATE=fresh npm --prefix web run dev`); unset, it is the prototype's dataset as today, and the built interface never reads the variable. One screenshot per screen in each state, taken with the pinned Playwright against that dev server at the two parity viewports, is saved under the git-ignored `work/fresh-install/`.

Writes over the new states are out of scope; so is any change to how a write is called.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The stand-in exports a fresh-install state and an empty-ledger state, and `createFakeApi({ state })` runs on each.
- [ ] Every answer of every `read` method over each of the two states validates against its result schema in the manifest.
- [ ] A sweep test mounts every route of `web/src/router.ts`, plus the transaction panel, a pot's page, an account's page, the card page and a subscription's page where the state has one, over both states: no error is thrown, no promise rejection is left unhandled, and the rendered text contains none of `NaN`, `undefined`, `Infinity`, `null`, `Invalid Date`.
- [ ] The chart geometry returns a finite height when the maximum is 0.
- [ ] A transaction with no line renders its row and its panel; a pot with no bucket renders in the list and on its page; the card page renders with no card.
- [ ] An unknown figure renders as a dash and never as `R$ 0,00`; a test asserts it for at least the last backup and an unknown yield.
- [ ] The prototype dataset is unchanged, and `npm --prefix web run parity` still reports every state at or under 0.05%.
- [ ] The manifest is regenerated and the gate's freshness check passes.
- [ ] No component gains a raw design value: `npm --prefix web run check:tokens` passes.
- [ ] `VITE_FINWISE_STATE=fresh` and `=empty` start the dev server's stand-in in those states; with the variable unset the prototype dataset is served, and the production build's output does not change with the variable set.
- [ ] One screenshot per screen for each state and each of the two parity viewports exists under `work/fresh-install/`, and the pull request lists every widened field with what its screen shows.

title: Derive the payday transfers from the month's budget under a stable key, mark one done by month and key, and let the pot page, the net worth and the budget follow
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, over their real bank data, the "Dia do salário" tab of the review shows the balance of the account
the salary lands on and nothing to do with it: the cushion reads R$ 0,00, the difference is a dash, the
list says "Nenhuma transferência planejada", a pot's page says "Sem aporte planejado" whatever the budget
plans for it, the net worth's "Aporte do mês" is two empty bars and the budget never shows the month's
investment as made. After this lands the tab says how much the account must hold before the salary is
set aside (the fixed and the variable lines of the month), whether the balance covers it and by how much,
and lists what to transfer on payday: one transfer for each pot the budget feeds, one for each provision
or reserve line that has no pot, and what is left to invest. "Marcar como feita" marks one of them for
the month on screen, dated today, and "Desfazer" takes it back. The pot's own page then says "Ainda não
feito" or "Feito em 20/03", the net worth shows how much of the month's plan is done and the real
investment rate, and the budget shows the investment as made. If this were wrong the person would see a
transfer for the wrong amount, a cushion that says "covered" when it is not, or, with two pots of the
same name, would mark one and find the other marked.

## Outcome
`PaydayTransfer` carries a `key`, and `review.markTransferDone` takes the month and that key. Over a
server with its own database, `review.payday(month)` answers the cushion, the balance, the difference
and the transfers derived from the budget in force for the month, each with its mark;
`review.markTransferDone` records a mark as one undoable change and answers null for a transfer that is
unknown or already marked; `savingsPots.detail` answers the pot's contribution state from the current
month's transfers; `netWorth.overview` answers the month's contribution and the investment rate from
them; `budget.view` answers the investment as made once its transfer is marked. The payday tab sends the
month it shows and the transfer's key, and the stand-in follows the two type changes and nothing else.
Without a database every one of these answers is what it is today.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it, through `internal/ledger`.
*The app's own database* is `finwise.db`: everything the person authors (a budget, a link between a
budget line and a pot, a mark) lives there and never in the snapshot. *The contract* is the TypeScript
interface `FinwiseApi` under `web/src/api/contract/`; *the manifest* is
`internal/contract/contract.json`, generated from it by `npm --prefix web run contract`, versioned and
never edited by hand, which gives Go each method's route, class and schemas. *The stand-in* is the
in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it and its tests are
the only existing statement of how writes behave, and its behaviour is the rule wherever this text does
not say otherwise. *The journal* is the record of every change made to authored data, which is what
makes a change undoable. *A pot* is what the pots screens list: a reserve entry of a bank account (id
`reserve:<account>/<reserveId>`), an investment (id `investment:<id>`) or, when the bank does not keep
an entry's identity stable, a slot (id `slot:<account>/<n>`). *A month* is `YYYY-MM` and *a day*
`YYYY-MM-DD`, both in Brazil time (`internal/brday`); "today" and "the current month" are the Brazil day
and month of the instant in the request's context, never of the host's clock. The budget has five
groups a person edits, by key: income (`rec`), fixed (`fix`), variable (`var`), provisions (`prov`) and
reserves (`res`). A provision is money set aside every month for a bill that comes once in a while; a
reserve is money set aside for something wanted.

**What earlier work provides.** None of this exists in the repository when this text is written; each
piece is delivered before this one and is used here as delivered.

- The app's own database ({{F1}}): the package `internal/authored`, which owns `finwise.db`, opens it
  when the server is started with `--db` / `FINWISE_DB`, applies its migrations by name and keeps every
  SQL statement over it as a registered constant; without `--db` the server is today's read-only server.
- The recorder ({{F2}}): the layer of `internal/authored` through which every change to a journaled
  table is written as one recorded change that `changes.undo` can take back. It knows two shapes of
  table; a *set table* holds rows that are facts by existing, and an effect on it is one row appearing
  or disappearing.
- The per-request views ({{F3b}}): a handler's third parameter is one value carrying a view of the
  ledger (one read-only transaction on the snapshot) and a view of the app's database (one read-only
  transaction, or an empty view that answers nothing when there is no database), and the clock is a
  required part of the configuration.
- Write dispatch ({{F4c}}): the router runs a registered write handler inside one transaction and one
  recorded change that it commits, after checking the arguments against the method's schema in the
  manifest; a write with no handler, or any write on a server without a database, answers `read_only`
  before its body is read; a test walks the manifest and requires every write to have a handler or be
  named in the list `writesWithoutHandler`, where `review.markTransferDone` stands until this slice.
- The write conformance harness ({{F5}}): a test requires a case for every write handler in its mode (a
  recorded change, whose effects are compared with a golden file under `testdata/golden/writes/` and
  whose undo must return a canonical dump of every journaled table to the dump taken before; or nothing
  to do, a null answer that adds no row to the journal), and the package
  `internal/authored/authoredtest` builds invented authored states for tests.
- The third read state ({{T1}}): the read conformance runs a third time over the full invented ledger
  with an invented authored state, with golden files in `testdata/golden/full-authored/` and cases in a
  list of their own, `authoredReadCases`.
- The budget's tables ({{B2}}): `lines(id, builtin)`, `budget_versions(from_month)`,
  `budget_version_lines(from_month, group_key, position, line_id, name, cents, flag)` and
  `closed_months(month, closed_on)`. A budget is a list of versions, each valid from a month on; the
  budget in force for a month is the latest version at or before it, and a month before the first
  version uses the first. A line has an integer id minted once and a name that belongs to the version.
- The budget view ({{B3}}): the pure package `internal/budgetrules`, whose `View` computes, in integer
  cents, the income, the investment as the residual (income less the fixed, variable, provision and
  reserve groups; it can be negative), the rate as a whole percent of the income and every cell of the
  budget screen, and the real `budget.view` with and without a draft. It answers the investment as "not
  made" until this slice.
- The pots' links ({{S2}}): the migration `0005_pots` with `pot_lines(line_id, pot_id)`, a line linked
  to at most one pot, and `pot_settings(pot_id, bucket)`; the write that toggles a link, refused for a
  `slot:` pot because its id changes between days; and the pots list, a pot's page and the net worth
  screen fetching again when something was written.
- The review's migration ({{V1}}): `0007_review`, which creates `transfer_marks(month, transfer_key,
  done_on)` beside `closing_steps(month, step)` and `dismissed_warnings(id)` and enters them in the
  recorder's registry as set tables. If the store functions that read and write a mark are not there
  yet, they are part of this slice, in the file of `internal/authored` that holds the review's tables.

One later piece reads what this slice builds: the closing view of the month ({{V3}}) will list its
contributions from the same transfers and marks, and count a provision or reserve line as made, for its
planned amount, when the transfer that carries it is marked for that month or the month is closed. So
the derivation and the read of a month's marks must be reachable from outside the payday handler.

**What the code is today (each point checked in the file named).**

- `web/src/api/contract/review-payday.ts`: `PaydayTransfer` is `{name, amount, state, doneOn,
  markedByHand}` with `TransferState = 'on-target' | 'done' | 'pending'`; `PaydayView` is `{cushion,
  balance, balanceLabel, difference, covered, transfers}`; `PaydayApi.markTransferDone(name: string)`
  answers `ChangeResult | null`, "Null when the transfer is unknown or already done". The manifest's
  entry for the method takes one string. `web/src/api/contract/classification.ts` classes it `write`
  and `review.payday` `read`.
- `web/src/api/fake/payday.ts`: the stand-in's cushion is the total of the `fix` group plus the total of
  the `var` group of the budget in force for the month asked; the salary account is the fixed id
  `'itau'`; the difference is the balance less the cushion and `covered` is `difference >= 0`; the
  transfers are a seeded list, `state.plannedContributions`, the same whatever month is asked.
  `markTransferDone(name)` finds one by name, answers null unless it is `pending`, and otherwise sets
  `state: 'done'`, `doneOn: state.shell.today`, `markedByHand: true` under one change.
  `FakePlannedContribution` in `model.ts` is `{name, amount, state, doneOn, markedByHand?}`; the seven
  seeded ones are in `prototype-data.ts` (`PLANNED_CONTRIBUTIONS`), in the budget's own order: one pot
  at its target, the three provision lines, the two reserve lines, then "Investimento".
- `web/src/api/fake/payday.test.ts` pins: cushion 6780 against a balance of 7020 gives a difference of
  240 and `covered: true`; a balance of 6000 gives -780 and false; a balance equal to the cushion is
  covered; raising a cap raises the cushion; a mark is dated today and `markedByHand`; a mark shows on
  the pot's page; a mark is taken back by its change; a done, an on-target and an unknown transfer
  answer null. `web/src/api/fake/closing.test.ts` also calls `markTransferDone('Compras')`.
- `web/src/api/fake/savings-rules.ts`: `plannedFor(state, pot)` is the first planned deposit, in list
  order, whose name is the pot's or, for a pot that is an investment, whose name is "Investimento".
  `potContribution` answers `closed` for a closed pot, `switched-off` for a pot at its target,
  `none-planned` with no planned deposit, `done` with its day, else `pending`. `potMovements` puts a
  synthetic row "Depósito · aporte do mês" in front of a pot's movements once its deposit is done.
  `monthContribution` is `planned` = provisions + reserves + the residual, `done` = the amounts of the
  done deposits, `progress` = `min(100, done / planned * 100)` as a fraction. `investmentRate` is the
  residual as a percent of the income as planned, and as actual the same once "Investimento" is done
  and zero before; both null when the budget has no income (`percentOfIncome` in `rules.ts`).
  `savings.test.ts` pins each of these.
- `web/src/api/fake/budget-view.ts`: `investmentMade(state, closed, investment)` is the whole residual
  when the "Investimento" deposit is done or the month is closed, and zero otherwise; `budget.test.ts`
  ("counts the investment as made once the deposit is, and in a closed month as whole") pins 0 for the
  open month, 3800 for the closed one and 3800 once the deposit is done.
- `internal/api/review_payday.go`: `readPayday` reads the accounts and every listed transaction and
  answers `paydayView` with `Cushion` zero, `Difference` and `Covered` always null and `Transfers` an
  empty list of `any`; its comment says why: with no budget there is nothing to compare the balance
  with. `findSalaryAccount` is the bank account with the latest payroll credit: a row of type `CREDIT`
  that is not `PENDING` and whose operation type is `FOLHA_PAGAMENTO` (`isSalaryCredit`), on an account
  of type `BANK`; on a tie of instants the lower account id wins. The balance answered is that
  account's current balance and the label is `bankAccountDescription` of its bank and name.
- `internal/api/review_payday_test.go`: `newSalariedLedger` builds an invented ledger with two bank
  accounts that each received a payroll credit and every shape that must not count; the chosen account
  has a balance of 777.77 and the label "Mercado Pago · Conta Salário", and the clock of the test is 20
  March 2026 (`fixtureNow`). Its comment says why it stays apart: a payroll row in the shared fixtures
  would change every golden file that lists transactions. The shared full ledger
  (`internal/api/fixtures_test.go`) has no payroll credit (`tx-salary` there is a received PIX), so over
  it the payday's balance is null: `review_test.go` pins that answer for both shared ledgers.
- `internal/api/pots_detail.go`: `contributionOf(entry)` answers `closed` for a closed entry and
  `none-planned` for every other; `potContributionWire` has only `State`. `accountSideDetail`, the page
  of a bank account's movements that no pot could claim, answers `none-planned`.
- `internal/api/net_worth.go`: `netWorth()` answers `Contribution: monthContributionWire{}` (planned
  0, done 0, progress 0; `Progress` is an `int`) and `InvestmentRate` with the current month and
  `Planned` and `Actual` null (both `*int`).
- `internal/api/pots_model.go`: `loadPots(ctx, reader, withYield)` builds the entries the pots screens
  list (`potEntry`: `id`, `name` nil for a pot the bank gives no name, `closed`, `investment` set for an
  investment); `sortedEntries` orders them comparing names with Go's plain string order. `withYield`
  false skips the yield computation, as `home.go` already asks.
- `internal/api/budget.go` and `budget_view.go`: today `budget.view` answers the empty groups and
  `investmentGroup()` answers the investment line's cells as `money 0`, `money 0`, percent unknown. The
  budget view's own slice replaces this before this one starts.
- `internal/api/messages.go` holds every text the server writes that a person reads, in Brazilian
  Portuguese; `budgetGroupInvestment` is "Investimento". The interface calls a pot the bank gives no
  name "Sem nome" (`PotRow.vue`, `CofrinhoScreen.vue`).
- `web/src/screens/revisao/PaydayTab.vue`: loads `api.review.payday(month.selected)` whenever the
  selected month or the revision counter changes; draws one row per transfer with `:key="transfer.name"`;
  `markDone` calls `api.review.markTransferDone(transfer.name)` and, on a non-null answer, announces
  `` `${transfer.name}: transferência marcada como feita.` `` through `useReviewActions().announce`,
  which bumps the revision and shows a toast with "Desfazer". Its test is
  `web/src/screens/revisao/payday.test.ts`; `web/scripts/parity/states.mjs` has the state
  `revisao-salario-transferencia-feita`, which clicks "Marcar como feita".
- `web/src/api/contract/manifest.test.ts` validates every answer of the stand-in's reads against the
  manifest's schemas, so a `PaydayTransfer` the stand-in answers without a `key` fails it.

**1. The contract.** `PaydayTransfer` gains a required `key: string`, the transfer's identity within
its month; `name` stays what the person reads. `PaydayApi.markTransferDone` becomes `(month: YearMonth,
key: string)` and keeps its result, null when the transfer is unknown or already done. The manifest is
regenerated. Nothing else of the contract changes: `TransferState` keeps `on-target` and
`PotContribution` keeps `switched-off`, which the stand-in answers for a pot at its target; the server
never answers either, because nobody can author a pot's target yet (a decision of the person, recorded
as: pot targets get no control for now, and no pot shows one).

**2. The transfers of a month.** They are derived, never stored. Lost with that decision: the
stand-in's seeded list, which has no rule behind it. The inputs, for a month M:

- the lines of the provisions group and of the reserves group of the budget in force for M, each with
  its line id, the name it has in that version and its amount in cents, in the budget's own order (the
  provisions group, then the reserves group, each line at its position). A line of any other group
  takes no part, linked or not;
- the links of `pot_lines`: for a line id, at most one pot id. A link is not of a month; it is what
  the person has linked now;
- the pots the ledger lists now, as `loadPots` builds them: each one's id, its name (nil when the bank
  gives none) and whether it is closed;
- the residual of M's budget, as the budget view computes it.

The rule:

1. A line's link counts only while the pot it names is listed by the ledger now and is open. A line
   linked to a pot that is closed, or that the ledger no longer has, is treated as linked to none.
2. One transfer per pot that has at least one counted link: key `pot:<pot id>`, the whole pot id after
   the prefix (`pot:reserve:acc-pots/pot-1`); amount, the sum of its linked lines' amounts; name, the
   pot's name, or "Sem nome" for a pot the bank gives no name.
3. One transfer per provision or reserve line linked to none: key `line:<line id>` (`line:14`);
   amount, the line's amount; name, the line's name in M's budget.
4. One transfer for the residual when it is above zero: key `investment`; amount, the residual; name,
   "Investimento". A residual of zero or below gives none.
5. A transfer of zero is not listed: a line of 0.00 linked to none, and a pot whose linked lines add up
   to 0.00.
6. Order: the pot transfers, by name and then by pot id; then the line transfers; then `investment`.
   The name compared is the one the transfer shows, so an unnamed pot sorts as "Sem nome", and the
   comparison is Go's plain string order, the one `sortedEntries` already uses for pot names. The line
   transfers keep the budget's own order (provisions before reserves, each at its position), which is
   also the order of the prototype's list. The rule as decided states only "pots by name and then id";
   these two readings complete it, and each has a row in the table test.

Every key is unique within a month, and stable: a line keeps its id through a rename, and a pot's id is
the bank's. Two pots of one name are therefore two transfers that differ only by key. Because every
provision and reserve line is carried by exactly one transfer or is zero, the pot and line transfers of
a month always add up to the total of the two groups; a property test holds that.

A worked example, all of it invented. The budget in force for 2026-03:

| group | line id | line | amount | linked to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| income | 1 | Salário | 8.000,00 | |
| fixed | 2 | Aluguel | 2.500,00 | |
| fixed | 3 | Internet | 120,00 | |
| variable | 4 | Mercado | 900,00 | |
| variable | 5 | Lazer | 300,00 | |
| provisions | 11 | IPTU | 150,00 | `reserve:acc-pots/pot-1`, open, named "Reserva" |
| provisions | 12 | Seguro do carro | 90,00 | `reserve:acc-pots/pot-1` |
| provisions | 13 | Presentes | 60,00 | `reserve:acc-nu/pot-nu-1`, open, also named "Reserva" |
| provisions | 14 | Revisão do carro | 200,00 | no pot |
| provisions | 15 | Material escolar | 0,00 | no pot |
| reserves | 16 | Viagem | 400,00 | `reserve:acc-nu/pot-nu-old`, closed |
| reserves | 17 | Celular novo | 250,00 | `reserve:acc-pots/pot-7`, open, no name from the bank |
| reserves | 18 | Bicicleta | 100,00 | `reserve:acc-gone/pot-x`, which the ledger no longer lists |

The cushion is 2.620,00 + 1.200,00 = 3.820,00. The residual is 8.000,00 - (2.620,00 + 1.200,00 + 500,00
+ 750,00) = 2.930,00. The transfers of 2026-03, in order:

| # | key | name | amount | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `pot:reserve:acc-nu/pot-nu-1` | Reserva | 60,00 | line 13; same name as the next, lower id first |
| 2 | `pot:reserve:acc-pots/pot-1` | Reserva | 240,00 | lines 11 and 12 added |
| 3 | `pot:reserve:acc-pots/pot-7` | Sem nome | 250,00 | line 17; the bank gives the pot no name |
| 4 | `line:14` | Revisão do carro | 200,00 | linked to no pot |
| 5 | `line:16` | Viagem | 400,00 | its pot is closed, so it is linked to none |
| 6 | `line:18` | Bicicleta | 100,00 | its pot is gone from the ledger, so it is linked to none |
| 7 | `investment` | Investimento | 2.930,00 | the residual, above zero |

Line 15 gives no transfer: its amount is zero. The seven add up to 4.180,00, which is 500,00 + 750,00 +
2.930,00. With the salary lowered to 5.000,00 the residual is -70,00: the first six transfers are
unchanged, there is no `investment` transfer, and the six add up to 1.250,00.

Where the pure function lives is the implementer's, within these bounds: it takes plain values and
returns plain values, opens nothing and knows no HTTP, as `internal/txrules`, `internal/cardrules` and
`internal/potrules` do today; `internal/budgetrules` is the natural home, since the residual and the
rate are that package's. No float and no `time.Now` may appear in it: the tests that forbid both cover
the rule packages.

**3. Marks, and `review.markTransferDone(month, key)`.** A transfer is done only when the person marked
it, for the month the screen shows: the ledger cannot yet attribute a movement to a pot (the balance
history is too young; attributing movements so that a transfer marks itself is deferred work that will
use the same table). A mark is one row of `transfer_marks(month, transfer_key, done_on)`, a fact by
existing, written through the recorder as a set-table effect. A month's marks are joined to its derived
list by key. A mark counts only while its transfer is listed: if the budget or a link changes so that
the month's list no longer has that key, the mark shows nowhere and counts for nothing. This slice adds
no cleanup: nothing removes a mark but the undo of the change that made it.

The write, in order:

1. The arguments are two strings (the router has already checked them against the manifest). The month
   is parsed through `internal/brday`; `2026-13` is `bad_request`, as the reads answer it.
2. Derive the transfers of that month, from the request's ledger view and the app's database as the
   write's own transaction sees it. A missing snapshot answers `ledger_unavailable`, through the same
   classifier as a read, and records nothing.
3. A key the month's list does not have answers null. A key whose transfer is already marked for that
   month answers null. Neither leaves a trace in the journal.
4. Otherwise record the mark with `done_on` = today, and answer `{"changeId": "<id>"}`. The change's
   author is the person and its method `review.markTransferDone`. It has no history step: a transfer is
   not a transaction.

`changes.undo` of that id removes the row; the transfer is pending again and can be marked again. None
of the contract's refusal reasons names this write: a closed month and a month other than the current
one are marked like any other, since closing a month freezes its budget and nothing else. The mark of
one month says nothing about another month, even when the same budget version is in force for both.

**4. `review.payday(month)`.** The cushion is the total of the fixed group plus the total of the
variable group of the budget in force for the month asked, in integer cents. The salary account, its
balance and its label are what `findSalaryAccount` and `readPayday` already answer, unchanged: the
account's current balance whatever month is asked, null when no account ever received a payroll
credit. The difference is the balance less the cushion, and `covered` is `difference >= 0`, so a
balance equal to the cushion is covered. Both are null when there is no balance, and both stay null,
with the cushion 0.00, when there is no budget for the month, as today: a cushion of zero that comes
from an absent budget is not a figure to compare a balance with. "No budget for the month" is read
here as: the budget in force for it has no line at all, which is also the state of a database where no
budget was ever saved and of a server without a database. It is the same condition the rest of the
write side uses for a month that cannot be worked yet (its line menu is empty and its pending reviews
wait). A budget that has lines but none in the fixed and variable groups is a budget: its cushion is
truly zero and the balance is compared with it.

Each transfer is answered as `{key, name, amount, state, doneOn, markedByHand}`: `state` is `pending`
with `doneOn` null and `markedByHand` false, or `done` with the mark's day and `markedByHand` true.
The server never answers `on-target`. The handler needs the pots only for their id, name and closed
flag: it asks `loadPots` without the yield.

**5. A pot's contribution state on its page (`savingsPots.detail`).** It follows the transfers of the
current month, whatever month the rest of the app is looking at:

- a closed pot: `{"state":"closed"}`, as today;
- an open pot for which the current month has no transfer: `{"state":"none-planned"}`;
- otherwise `{"state":"pending"}`, or `{"state":"done","doneOn":"<day>"}` once the transfer is marked.

The transfer of a pot is `pot:<its id>`. An investment (an entry whose `investment` is set, id
`investment:<id>`, whatever bucket the person gave it) follows the `investment` transfer, so every open
investment shares that one deposit, as in the stand-in's test "shares an investment deposit between
every investment". An investment that also has a transfer of its own, because a line is linked to it,
follows its own: the stand-in's `plannedFor` takes the first match in list order, and in the server's
order a pot's transfer comes before `investment`. A `slot:` pot cannot be linked, so its page says
`none-planned`. `accountSideDetail` is not a pot and keeps `none-planned`. `switched-off` is never
answered. The manifest's `PotContribution` is a union whose members other than `done` have no other
field, so `doneOn` is absent, not null, in them.

The page's movements come from the ledger only. The stand-in's synthetic "Depósito · aporte do mês" is
not ported: a mark is the person's word that a transfer was made, not a movement the bank reported, and
the real deposit is already in the ledger's rows.

**6. The net worth's contribution and investment rate (`netWorth.overview`).** Both are of the current
month. `contribution.planned` is the sum of the amounts of the current month's transfers;
`contribution.done` is the sum of the amounts of the marked ones; `contribution.progress` is `done *
100 / planned` as a whole number rounded half up, capped at 100, and 0 when nothing is planned.
`investmentRate.month` is the current month, as today; `planned` is the budget's rate of the current
month exactly as the budget view answers it (a whole percent, negative when the budget outgrows its
income, null when the budget has no income), taken from the same function and never recomputed here;
`actual` is that same rate once the `investment` transfer is marked, 0 before, and null when `planned`
is null. With a residual of zero or below there is no `investment` transfer to mark, so `actual` is 0.

Two things differ from the stand-in's arithmetic and are meant. Its `planned` adds the residual even
when negative; here a negative residual is not a transfer and takes nothing off the plan. Its
`progress` is a fraction (6.13 for 320 done of 5220); here it is the whole number 6, as every
percentage the server computes is.

**7. The budget view's "made" (`budget.view`).** The investment line's second cell is the residual
itself when the `investment` transfer of the month asked is listed and marked, or when that month is
closed (a closed month is taken as wholly made, as the stand-in's `investmentMade` does, whatever the
residual's sign), and 0.00 otherwise. With a draft, the residual and the transfer are the draft's: a
draft whose residual is zero or below has no `investment` transfer, so a mark made earlier does not
count. If the budget view already takes "made" as an input, this slice feeds it; if it does not, adding
that input is part of this slice. This read needs no pot: the `investment` transfer depends only on
the residual.

**8. The interface.** `PaydayTab.vue` keys its rows by `transfer.key`, and `markDone` sends the month
the list on screen was loaded for and the transfer's key. Keep that month beside the loaded view: the
selected month can change while a list of another month is still drawn, and a key of one month must
never be sent with another. The toast, the "Desfazer" action, the row's texts ("Pendente", "Feita em
20/03 · marcada por você") and the empty state do not change. The tab's hint, "O app marca como feita
quando encontra a transferência. Você também pode marcar à mão.", is the prototype's text and stays as
it is, although the app does not yet mark anything by itself. Call sites do not catch: a refused or
failed mark ends in `web/src/api/failures.ts` like every other write.

The stand-in follows the two type changes and nothing else. `FakePlannedContribution` gains a `key`,
the seeded seven get one each, `payday()` answers it and `markTransferDone(month, key)` finds by key.
The stand-in's list has no month, as its `payday(month)` already answers the same list for every
month; the new month argument is accepted and ignored. The key strings of the seeded transfers are the
implementer's: non-empty, unique in the list, the same on every call; the server's forms are not
required of them. Its tests that call the method (`payday.test.ts`, `closing.test.ts`) follow the new
signature and keep what they pin.

**Money and numbers.** Every amount is integer cents (`internal/money`) from the budget's `cents`
column to the wire, where `api.Reais` writes it; no source file of `internal/api` or of a rule package
may touch a float, and a test fails if one does. The only percentage this slice computes itself is the
contribution's progress, whose rounding is stated above; a row with an exact half pins it (1 done of 8
planned is 12.5 and answers 13).

**Decisions, with what lost.**

- The transfers are derived from the month's budget, keyed, and marked per month. Lost: a stored list
  of planned contributions like the stand-in's seeded one, which nothing would keep in step with the
  budget; marking by name, which cannot tell two pots of one name apart; one global mark, which would
  show March's transfer as done in April.
- A line's pot is the pot it is linked to in `pot_lines`, never a pot of the same name. Lost: the
  stand-in's join by name (`plannedFor`), under which renaming a line or a pot silently moves a
  deposit.
- A transfer is done only by hand. Lost: finding the movement in the ledger, which waits for a longer
  balance history.

**Where the server departs from the stand-in on purpose.** Transfers derived from the budget, keyed
and marked per month, instead of a seeded list marked by name. A pot's page shows no synthetic deposit.
The contribution's progress is a whole number. A negative residual plans no investment. Each is pinned
by a test, and the final report names the test beside each.

**Failure paths this slice owns.**

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the snapshot is missing while marking | `ledger_unavailable`; nothing is recorded |
| the mark fails halfway, or waits out the database's lock | one transaction: nothing of it is kept; `internal` |
| two tabs mark the same transfer | the writes queue; the first records the mark, the second answers null |
| the undo of a mark meets nothing later on the same row | the row is removed; a second undo of the same change is refused as stale by the undo engine |
| the budget or a link changes after a mark | the mark stays stored; it counts only while its key is in the month's list |
| a pot is closed or leaves the ledger | its lines become line transfers under `line:<id>`; a mark under `pot:<id>` no longer counts |
| the server has no database | every answer here is today's; the write answers `read_only` |

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. A real
snapshot may be opened read-only to check a schema, the keys of a JSON column or a count; no value from
it (amount, description, name, document, id) is ever printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a
bead or a pull request; a count may be shown to the person running the test and goes into no file; a
test that touches a real ledger runs only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file. Nothing in this
slice needs one: every ledger and every authored state here is invented, including the pot names and
the amounts of the example above. A pot's name and a line's name are the person's own words: new files
of `internal/api` log nothing, and the request log keeps to verb, route, status, duration and error
kind.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of its own and ends at local commits: atomic,
Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit
message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path. Every SQL statement over the
app's database is a registered constant of `internal/authored`, the only package that executes SQL
against `finwise.db`. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; the texts
the server writes ("Sem nome", "Investimento") live in `internal/api/messages.go`. A design value in a
component comes from a token; this slice changes no style. The manifest is regenerated with `npm
--prefix web run contract`, never edited by hand; a conflict in it is settled by regenerating, never by
merging. A read handler that is registered needs its conformance cases and golden files; a golden file
changes only with `go test ./internal/api -run TestEveryAnswerMatchesItsGoldenFile -update`, which
refuses to run while `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set, and every changed golden file is read before it
is committed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `PaydayTransfer` has a required `key: string` and `PaydayApi.markTransferDone` is `(month:
YearMonth, key: string)`; `npm --prefix web run contract:check` passes, and `git diff` of
`internal/contract/contract.json` shows only the `PaydayTransfer` definition and the arguments of
`review.markTransferDone`, now two strings.
- [ ] The pure derivation, given the example's budget, links and pots, returns exactly the seven
transfers of the table above, in that order, with those keys, names and amounts in cents (6000, 24000,
25000, 20000, 40000, 10000, 293000); with the salary at 5.000,00 it returns the first six and no
`investment`.
- [ ] Its table test has a row for each of: two pots of one name (two transfers, lower pot id first); a
pot with two linked lines (one transfer, the sum); a pot with no name ("Sem nome", sorted under that
name); a line linked to no pot; a line linked to a closed pot; a line linked to a pot that is not
listed; a line of 0.00; a pot whose linked lines add up to 0.00; a residual of exactly 0.00 (no

an empty budget (no transfer).
- [ ] For generated budgets, links and pots, the keys of a month's transfers are all different, no
transfer is zero, and the amounts of the pot and line transfers add up to the total of the provisions

- [ ] Over the salaried invented ledger (`newSalariedLedger`, balance 777.77, label "Mercado Pago ·
Conta Salário") with an invented budget in force for 2026-03, `review.payday(["2026-03"])` answers:
with a cushion of 700.00, `difference` 77.77 and `covered` true; with 777.77, `difference` 0.00 and

title: Add `finwise backup`, a checked copy that never replaces a file, and show the last backup in the settings
description:
## What changes for the user
Once the app keeps what a person types, that one file is the only copy of months of decisions about
their money, and nothing today can copy it safely: copying the file by hand while the app is running
can produce a copy that looks whole and is missing the latest changes. The settings screen already
has a line "Último backup:", and it always shows a dash. After this lands there is one command that
takes a complete, checked copy while the app keeps running and never writes over a copy that is
already there, and the settings line says when the last one was taken ("hoje às 02:15", or the date).
If this were wrong the person would find out on the worst day: a backup that cannot be restored, or
one that silently replaced the last good copy.

## Outcome
`finwise backup --db <file> --to <file>` writes a consistent copy of the app's database: it
recognises the source by its first hundred bytes before touching it and treats a missing or empty one
as an error, copies with `VACUUM INTO` to a temporary file beside the destination, checks the copy,
publishes it with an operation that cannot replace a file, and then records the instant in the source
database. A destination that exists, or appears meanwhile, is refused and untouched; no temporary
file outlives a failure; and if the instant cannot be recorded the copy just published is removed, so
a backup and its record exist together or not at all. `settings.overview` answers that instant as
`lastBackup`, in Brazil time, and null while no backup has run or no database is configured.

## Context
finwise is a personal finance app for one person. The **ledger** is a SQLite snapshot that a separate
collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. The **app's own database**,
`finwise.db`, holds everything the person authors, and `internal/authored` is the only package that
executes SQL against it. The collector can always fetch the ledger again; what is in `finwise.db`
exists nowhere else, which is why it needs a backup of its own.

**What exists when this starts.** Two pieces of earlier work have landed; read the code as it is,
since file and function names are whatever that work chose.

- The work that creates the database ({{F1}}): `internal/authored` recognises a file by its first
  hundred bytes before writing to it, opens it with fixed connection settings (`foreign_keys(1)`,
  `busy_timeout(5000)`, `synchronous(FULL)`, `journal_mode(WAL)`, immediate write transactions),
  applies migrations, keeps every statement as a registered constant that a test prepares against the
  migrated schema, and created the table `meta(key, value)`, which holds the month the database was
  created in and is where the instant of the last backup goes. `finwise serve --db` keeps the database
  open for the life of the server. The clock is a required part of the configuration, and
  `environment` in `cmd/finwise/main.go` carries it: the host's in `main`, a fixed one in a test.
- The work that gives every handler a view of each store per request, and makes the clock required
  and guarded in the API ({{F3b}}): a read handler's third parameter, today a `*ledger.Reader`
  (`ReadHandler` in `internal/api/reads.go`), is one value carrying a view of the ledger and a view of
  the app's database, the latter inside one read-only transaction opened for the request. Without
  `--db` that view is an empty one that answers nothing, so read code has one path.

**Recognition, as `serve` does it, with one exception.** Recognition does not open the file as a
database: it reads the file's first hundred bytes, which must be the header of an SQLite file carrying
the application id finwise stamps, `0x46494E57` (decimal 1179209303; bytes 68 to 71 of the header, big
endian). Any other file, the collector's snapshot included, is refused with its bytes untouched and no
file created beside it. Use the package's recognition, do not write a second one. The exception: for
`serve` a file that does not exist or is empty is a new database, which it creates; here a missing or
empty file is an error and is never created. A mistyped path must not leave a database behind, nor fix
the month a person "started" in it. This command also never runs a migration.

**The copy.** After recognition the command writes a consistent copy, in this order:

1. `VACUUM INTO` a uniquely named temporary file in the destination's directory. The same directory
   is what makes the last step possible; `VACUUM INTO` reads one consistent state of the source even
   while the server is writing to it, and it refuses a file that already holds anything.
2. Check the temporary file: its application id, and `PRAGMA integrity_check`.
3. Publish it with an operation that cannot replace a file: a hard link to the destination name, then
   removing the temporary name. A rename would replace whatever is at the destination; a link fails
   when the name is taken, which is the whole reason it is used.
4. On success, record the instant, from the injected clock, in the source database, as UTC in
   RFC 3339. If that record cannot be written, remove the copy just published and fail.

A destination that exists before, or appears meanwhile, is refused and untouched; every failure
removes only this command's temporary file. The one file besides the temporary one that the command
may ever remove is the copy it has itself just published, in the one case of step 4: a backup and its
record exist together or not at all. It never removes or replaces a file it did not publish in this
run. A plain file copy of a running database is not supported, because it can miss the write-ahead
log; the nightly backup of the later packaging work calls this command.

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| a backup's destination exists or appears meanwhile | refused; the destination and the database are untouched; no temporary file is left |
| `--db` points at a file that is not ours | refused; file untouched, no side file created |
| `--db` is missing or empty | an error; the file is not created |
| the instant cannot be recorded after the copy was published | the published copy is removed; the command fails |

All SQL here (`VACUUM INTO`, the two checks of the copy, the write to `meta`) is executed by
`internal/authored` through registered constants; `cmd/finwise` parses the flags, calls it and
reports. `VACUUM` cannot run inside a transaction. The check of the copy must not leave a `-wal`,
`-shm` or `-journal` file beside the published destination.

**The command line.** `run` in `cmd/finwise/main.go` knows `serve` and `hash-pin` and prints
`usage: finwise serve | hash-pin` in two places; `backup` joins both. The existing exit constants are
`exitFailure` (1) and `exitUsage` (2); `runServe` prints `finwise: <error>` to standard error. The
source is resolved the way `serve` resolves it, the flag `--db` first and then `FINWISE_DB`
(`firstNonEmpty` in `cmd/finwise/serve.go`), so the nightly job can run in the server's own
environment; `--to` is a flag only. Both a source and a destination are required. A message names a
path and a fixed reason, never the content of a
file: a raw SQLite error can quote a value, so errors carry fixed sentences, as
`UnreadableSnapshotError` in `internal/ledger/open.go` does.

**The settings read.** The instant recorded is what the settings screen's "last backup" shows, in
Brazil time like the last sync. Today `dataSettingsOf` (`internal/api/settings_data.go`) fills
`LastSync` as `momentWire{Day: string(brday.DayOf(finished)), Time: clockTimeOf(finished)}` and never
fills `LastBackup`; its comment says "This backend makes no backup, so there is none to show", and
`TestTheSettingsReportTheLastCompleteRunAndNoBackup` (`settings_test.go`) expects null.
`dataSettingsWire` in `settings.go` already has the field, and the contract already types it
(`DataSettings.lastBackup: Moment | null`, "Null when no backup has run", in
`web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`; `Moment` is a day and a time). The instant is stored as UTC in
RFC 3339 and shown in Brazil time: it is read through the request's view of the app's database and
written on the wire the same way as the last sync, the Brazil day and the time as `HH:MM`. With no
instant recorded, or no database configured, it stays null.

Nothing changes in `web/`: `web/src/screens/config/DataSection.vue` already prints
"Último backup: hoje às 02:15" for today, "Último backup: em 26/11 às 02:15" for another day and
"Último backup: —" for null, and its tests (`config.test.ts`, `web/src/test/first-run-fields.test.ts`)
already cover the three. The golden files `internal/api/testdata/golden/empty/settings.overview.json`
and `full/settings.overview.json` are answered without a database and keep `"lastBackup": null`. Do
not add a `readCase{…}` literal for a state with a backup: `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts` scans
every `_test.go` file of `internal/api` for those literals and requires each to have a golden file in
`empty/`. The read with a recorded instant is a test of its own.

**Left to the implementer.** No criterion below leaves a number or a representation open. What is
free is mechanism: the key under which the instant sits in `meta`, which is the package's, since
nothing outside the package reads `meta` by key; how a test makes a destination appear between the
checks and the publication (a hook, or two functions the test calls in turn), as long as the file
really is created after the destination was found free and before the link; and how a test makes the
record of the instant fail after the publication, as long as the copy really was published first.

**Privacy and conventions.** A backup is a whole copy of what a person authored. No test here touches
a real ledger or a real database: sources are created in temporary directories with invented
content, and the "collector's snapshot" of the refusal test is the invented one `ledgertest.New`
builds. The command prints paths and fixed sentences only. Work happens in the worktree it was given
and ends at local commits: atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a
session, a work item or a plan in a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in
the money path. Every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant. Interface text
is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is English; a design value in a component comes from a
token (no component is touched here). `internal/authored` and `internal/api` log nothing here, and
`internal/api` reads the clock only from the request, never from the host.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `finwise backup --db <db> --to <dest>` over a database created by the package exits 0. `<dest>`
then carries application id 1179209303, answers `ok` to `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and holds the same
rows of `schema_migrations` and the same creation month as the source.
- [ ] After a success the destination's directory has gained exactly one entry, `<dest>`: no temporary
file and no `-wal`, `-shm` or `-journal` beside it.
- [ ] After a success with the clock at 2026-12-01T01:30:00Z, the instant stored in the source is the
RFC 3339 text `2026-12-01T01:30:00Z`, and `settings.overview` over that database answers
`"lastBackup": {"day":"2026-11-30","time":"22:30"}`. A second backup with the clock at
2026-12-02T05:15:00Z makes it `{"day":"2026-12-02","time":"02:15"}`.
- [ ] `settings.overview` answers `"lastBackup": null` over a database in which no backup was
recorded, and without a database. `git diff` shows no change under `internal/api/testdata/golden/`.
- [ ] A destination that exists before the command runs: the exit is non-zero, the destination's
SHA-256 is equal before and after, the source's SHA-256 is equal before and after, no instant is
recorded, and the destination's directory listing is equal before and after.
- [ ] A destination created after the command found the name free and before it publishes: the exit is
non-zero, the file that appeared is byte-identical afterwards, no instant is recorded, and the only
new entry in the directory is the file that appeared.
- [ ] Each failure the tests can force after the temporary file exists (the copy's check failing, the
link failing) leaves no temporary file.
- [ ] When the record of the instant fails after the copy was published (forced by the test), the exit
is non-zero, the published copy is gone, no instant is recorded, and the destination's directory
listing is equal to what it was before the command.
- [ ] Given as `--db`, each of these is refused with a non-zero exit, its SHA-256 and its directory
listing equal before and after, and no destination created: a foreign database in write-ahead mode;
an invented collector snapshot built by `ledgertest`; a database with one table and application id 1;
a text file that is not a database.
- [ ] A `--db` that does not exist is an error and is not created. A zero-byte `--db` is an error, is
still zero bytes afterwards, and leaves nothing in the destination's directory.
- [ ] A copy taken while another connection commits transactions of two rows each, in a loop, passes
both checks and holds an even number of those rows.
- [ ] A backup changes nothing in the source but the one recorded instant: `schema_migrations`, the
creation month and every other row read the same before and after.
- [ ] `FINWISE_DB` supplies the source when `--db` is absent, and the flag wins when both are given.
With neither, or without `--to`, the command exits with the usage status and touches no file; no
variable stands in for `--to`. `finwise` with no argument names `backup` in its usage line.
- [ ] A sentinel string stored in the source (invented, for example as a `method` in `changes`) appears
in neither stream of the command, on success and on every refusal above.
- [ ] Every statement added to `internal/authored` is a registered constant: the package's
registration and preparation tests pass with them and fail when one is left out.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, and the report names the break used for each: the link
replaced by a rename (a destination that exists, and one that appears, are both replaced); the removal
of the temporary file dropped; the instant recorded before the publication (a refusal then shows an
instant); the published copy left in place when the record of the instant fails; the check of the
copy skipped; the database opened the way `serve` opens it (a missing or empty `--db` becomes a
database); the settings read left at null.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, a copy taken during a write passes its checks, the
settings read shows the recorded instant, and a destination that exists or appears is not replaced.

## Tests
- Integration, `cmd/finwise`, in a new `backup_test.go` that uses the existing `runCommand` of
`finwise_test.go` with the injected clock, over temporary directories: the success and what the
directory holds after it; the source taken from `FINWISE_DB` and the flag winning over it; the usage
errors; the refusals of a source that is not ours, missing or empty, each with hashes and directory
listings; the sentinel in the output.
- Unit, `internal/authored`, over temporary files: the destination that exists; the destination that
appears between the checks and the publication; no temporary file after each forced failure; the
record of the instant failing after the publication, and the copy removed with it; the instant
recorded only on success, as RFC 3339 in UTC, and replaced by the next backup; the source otherwise
unchanged.
- Unit, `internal/authored`, two connections on one temporary file: the copy taken during a loop of
committed writes.
- Unit, `internal/api`, over the invented full ledger of `fixtures_test.go` and a temporary database:
`settings.overview` with an instant recorded on each side of midnight in Brazil, with none recorded,
and with no database.
- Golden: `settings.overview` over the two fixture ledgers, unchanged.
- Unit, source scans: the new statements registered and prepared.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `cmd/finwise/backup.go`, `cmd/finwise/backup_test.go`, `cmd/finwise/main.go`,
`internal/authored/`, `internal/api/settings_data.go`, `internal/api/settings.go`,
`internal/api/settings_test.go`
**Reads only:** `cmd/finwise/finwise_test.go`, `cmd/finwise/serve.go`, `internal/authored/migrations/`,
`internal/api/reads.go`, `internal/api/now.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/`,
`internal/ledger/ledgertest/`, `web/src/api/contract/settings.ts`,
`web/src/screens/config/DataSection.vue`, `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`, `bin/ci`

A new command file and its line in `main.go`; in `internal/authored` the copy, its checks, the
publication, and the write and read of one `meta` value; in `internal/api` the one field of the
settings read. About six code files, most of them small, but in three packages, which is what makes it
`size:L` on the scale. No migration is added (`meta` exists), nothing in `web/` changes, and no golden
file changes.

## Recovery path
A backup that should not have been taken is undone by deleting the destination file. The command
itself never replaces a file, and the only copy it ever removes is the one it has just published when
it cannot record the instant. The instant it recorded stays in the database and only says when a copy
was last taken; the next backup replaces it. To restore the database from a backup: stop
the server; check the copy (`PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok`, the application id is
1179209303); put it in place of the database with no `-wal` or `-shm` file beside it; start the
server. A restore does not set the creation month again: the copy carries the one it was taken with.

title: Read pluggy-sync's snapshot through typed read-only queries
description:
## What changes for the user
Today everything finwise shows is an invented dataset; none of it is the person's own money. This is the first piece that reads the real ledger the collector writes every night. Nothing looks different on screen once it lands, but the app gains a tested way to ask that ledger for accounts, transactions, card bills, savings pots, investments and the state of the last synchronisation, and it refuses a ledger whose format it does not know instead of showing wrong numbers.

## Outcome
A Go module at the repository root (`github.com/gabrielassisxyz/finwise`) with a package that opens pluggy-sync's snapshot file strictly read-only for each call, pins its schema version, and answers typed queries over the documented surface only. It ships with the fixture builder every later Go test uses, a test that prepares every query against the real schema, an opt-in test over a real snapshot that reports counts only, and the Go toolchain joined to the gate and to CI.

## Context
finwise has no backend yet. `web/` is a Vue interface running on an in-memory stand-in. The backend will be one Go binary; this bead starts it and contains no HTTP.

**The ledger.** pluggy-sync is the separate, public collector that pulls bank data into SQLite every night. Beside its live database it publishes `pluggy-snapshot.db`: a verified copy written to a temporary file and swapped in by an atomic rename, mode 0600, journal mode `delete`. A reader uses the snapshot and never the live file. Nothing promises what an open handle sees across a swap, so the reader opens read-only, runs its query and closes, on every call.

**Version.** `PRAGMA user_version` is 1 today. The collector promises nothing to readers about it, so the reader accepts exactly 1 and returns a typed error for anything else, before any query runs.

**Surface.** Only this is stable: the nine current-state tables (`items`, `accounts`, `transactions`, `bills`, `investments`, `investment_transactions`, `consents`, `identities`, `categories`), the views listed in pluggy-sync's README, `daily_sightings` (used by a README query) and `runs`. Anything else is internal to the collector and must not be queried.

**What exists now.** On every current-state table a row is current when `state = 'present' AND ambiguous_run IS NULL`.

**The clean list of transactions** is a README query, not a view: the predicate above, joined to `document_coverage` with `covered = 1`, minus every `PENDING` row whose id appears in `pending_posted_candidates.pending_id` (the collector's heuristic pairing of a pending row with the posted row that replaced it). Copy the query and cite the README lines in a comment beside it; the README of the checkout at dispatch has it near lines 287-296.

**Transactions.** Columns are `id, account_id, date, description, amount, currency, type, category, raw`. Everything else lives in the `raw` JSON: `status` (`PENDING` or `POSTED`), `operationType`, `amountInAccountCurrency`, `currencyCode`, `descriptionRaw`, `paymentData` (`paymentMethod`, and `payer` and `receiver`, each with `name` and `documentNumber.value`) and `creditCardMetadata` (`cardNumber`, `billId`, `installmentNumber`, `totalInstallments`, `purchaseDate`, `billForecastDate`, `feeType`, `payeeMCC`). The `merchant` column is null on every row. `date` is a UTC timestamp on every row.

**Accounts and bills.** `accounts.type` is `BANK` or `CREDIT`. A card's limit, available limit, closing and due dates are in `accounts.raw.creditData`. The bank behind an account is told by `accounts.name` or the first segment of `accounts.raw.bankData.transferNumber`; the connector name is the same for every bank. `bills` has `due_date`, `closing_date`, `total_amount`, `minimum_payment`.

**Pots.** `reserved_balance_history` has one row per reserve entry of an account's latest sighting of a day. A pot's key is `reserve_id`, valid only when `stable_identity = 1`; names repeat across pots. The latest balance of each pot is the README query `reserves_as_of` (near lines 239-258); nothing is carried forward from an earlier day.

**Investments.** `investment_history` has one row per investment per day with `amount_gross`, `taxes`, `taxes2`, `amount_net`, `rate`, `due_date`, `status`. `amountOriginal` is never summed.

**Synchronisation.** The last sync is `max(finished_at)` over `runs` with `outcome = 'complete'`; a later run may be `partial`. A connection is in trouble when `items.status != 'UPDATED'`, `execution_status != 'SUCCESS'`, or its last update is older than 48 hours. `consents.expires_at` and `revoked_at` are null in practice; the expiry is `items.raw.consentExpiresAt`.

**Money and days.** Amounts arrive as floating point out of JSON. The reader converts every amount to integer cents (round half away from zero) at its boundary, so no caller ever adds floats. A period is given in Brazil days and converted to UTC bounds inside the reader, because a row at 02:30 UTC on the 1st belongs to the last day of the previous month in America/Sao_Paulo.

**Scope.** The reader returns rows faithfully and interprets nothing: what kind a transaction is, the sign convention of the app, taxes folded into purchases and the card's bill rules belong to later beads. Its types must still carry every field named above, parsed, so those beads never touch SQL.

**Privacy, the rule above all others.** The ledger is a real person's complete financial history and this repository is public. A real snapshot may be opened read-only to check schema, JSON keys and counts. No value from it is ever printed, copied, logged, committed or pasted. Every fixture and every test uses invented literals.

**Decided, with what lost.** `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go, keeps one static binary) over the cgo driver. Reopening per call over a long-lived handle, because of the rename. Copying README queries with a citation over views added to the collector, which would change its schema version and need a release there; that is revisited once the queries have proven themselves.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `go test ./...` passes from the repository root with no environment variable set and writes nothing outside the tests' temporary directories.
- [ ] A fixture whose `user_version` is 2 yields the typed unsupported-version error from every query and no rows.
- [ ] The snapshot is opened read-only: a test attempts a write through the same open path and it fails, and the fixture file's SHA-256 is identical before and after running every query.
- [ ] A test replaces the fixture file by rename between two calls and the second call returns the new content.
- [ ] The clean list, over a fixture holding one row of each case (state not `present`, `ambiguous_run` set, not covered, `PENDING` with a posted pair, `PENDING` without a pair, `POSTED`), returns exactly the unpaired pending row, the posted row and the posted half of the pair.
- [ ] A transaction dated `2026-03-01T02:30:00Z` is returned for February 2026 and not for March 2026.
- [ ] `19.99` becomes 1999 cents, `-0.005` becomes -1, and a sum of one thousand rows of `0.10` is exactly 10000.
- [ ] The consent expiry is read from `items.raw.consentExpiresAt`; a fixture with `consents.expires_at` null and that key set returns the key's value.
- [ ] `internal/ledger/testdata/ledger-schema-v1.sql` is the collector's real schema, a test asserts it contains no `INSERT`, and a test prepares every query of the package against a database built from it. Renaming one selected column in any query makes that test fail.
- [ ] A test skipped unless `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set runs every query over that file and logs row counts only.
- [ ] `bin/ci` runs `gofmt -l` (failing on any output), `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go build ./...`, and still ends with `CI green.`; the workflow installs the Go version named in `go.mod`; every existing step is unchanged.
- [ ] `go.mod` requires `modernc.org/sqlite` and nothing else directly.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` describes the Go side under "Stack & Commands" and states the real-ledger rule under "Tests".
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` on the branch and the opt-in run over a real snapshot completes with counts and no error.

## Tests
- Unit: cents conversion and rounding; Brazil-day and month bounds, including the daylight-free UTC-3 offset at month and year ends.
- Unit over synthetic fixtures: one test per query, each asserting the exact rows returned for a fixture that also holds rows that must be excluded.
- Unit: version refusal, read-only open, file hash unchanged, rename between calls.
- Golden: the schema file against every prepared query.
- Integration, opt-in: the whole query set over a real snapshot, counts only.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `internal/ledger/`, `internal/money/`, `internal/brday/`, `bin/ci`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/contract/`

Three small Go packages, all new: `internal/ledger` (the reader, its `ledgertest` fixture builder exported for other packages' tests, and its `testdata`), `internal/money` (integer cents) and `internal/brday` (a day and a month in Brazil time). The gate and the workflow gain Go steps and keep every existing one. Nothing under `web/` changes.
close_reason: internal/ledger opens the snapshot read-only on every call (mode=ro plus query_only), pins user_version 1 with a typed error, and answers accounts, the clean list, bills, pots, investments, identities and the sync state; internal/money holds integer cents and internal/brday gives Brazil days as UTC bounds. Every statement lives in one registry that a test prepares against the collector's real schema. bin/ci: CI green with the four Go steps. The opt-in run over a real snapshot completed with counts and no error. Correction to the bead text: the transactions table has no merchant column at all, rather than a column that is always null.

title: Use the read-only app at the desktop on the real ledger
description:
## What changes for the user
For the first time the person opens finwise and sees their own money in it, at their own desk, instead of a designer's example. Everything the app shows about the bank's records gets a first look from the only one who can tell whether it is right, before anything that changes data is designed on top of it.

## Outcome
The user has used the read-only app at the desktop on a copy of the real ledger, and what was wrong or surprising is written down as beads.

## Context
finwise's interface was ported from a design and measured against it pixel by pixel, on an invented dataset; no person has ever opened it. Its backend reads the bank's records through rules that turn raw rows into the list a person expects: signs, purchases abroad, tax rows folded under their purchase, transfers between own accounts set apart, savings-pot movements out of the general list, the card's closing date, each pot's yield. Several of those rules were written where the sources were silent, and each reports how many rows it matched; only the person can say whether the result is right.

The part of the app that stores what the person authors (budget, categorisation, tags, subscriptions, closing a month) has no plan yet. That plan is the next piece of work, and it starts from what this first use shows. One finding already waits for it: the bank's records carry no merchant on any row, so the establishment of a card purchase is derived from its text.

This check runs at the desktop on purpose. Packaging the app as one binary and putting it on the home server come after the write side, so that the deployment is designed once.

**How to run it.** With a copy of the collector's snapshot at hand:

```sh
go build -o finwise ./cmd/finwise
printf '%s' '<six digits>' | ./finwise hash-pin        # prints the hash
FINWISE_PIN_HASH='<the hash>' ./finwise serve --ledger <path to pluggy-snapshot.db> --dev-insecure-cookie
npm --prefix web run dev:backend                        # in another terminal
```

Then open the address the dev server prints and unlock with the PIN.

**What to look at.** Início for two or three different months: is every purchase there once, is a purchase abroad in reais with its tax under it, are transfers between own accounts set apart. Contas and one account's page. The card page: the closing date, the due date, the amount that falls on the next bill. Cofrinhos: balances and yield against the bank's app. Patrimônio: the total against the sum the person knows. Budget, Assinaturas, Revisão and Configuração open empty, and trying to change anything says the app is read-only.

**Rules to confirm while looking.** Each of these was written where the sources were silent, and only the person can say whether the result is right:
- A debit on a bank account whose text starts with the bank's bill-payment wording is the payment of the card bill, shown as a movement and not as spending.
- A credit on the card with no operation type whose text names a payment is also a bill payment. Without the rule it would read as income.
- A card credit carrying a refund, cancellation or return word is a refund.
- A tax row named after its purchase is folded under it when it is 3.5% of the purchase, on the same card, within 3 days.
- An explicit international tax row is folded under a purchase abroad only when that card has exactly one such purchase that day. The others stay listed on their own: look for them on the cards that are no longer in use, and say whether they should attach by another key.
- A handful of rows no rule recognises are listed as ordinary transactions under "Outros".
- A card purchase with no bill id is placed on the first bill that closes after it; on a card with no known closing rule its bill is unknown.
- A savings pot counts as reserved and an investment as invested in the net worth until a bucket can be assigned.
- A deposit or withdrawal is attached to a pot only when exactly one pot can claim it; with only a few weeks of nightly balances most past movements stay on the account.

No real amount, name or document from the ledger goes into a bead, a commit or a screenshot attached anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria
