  with `onlyMonthArgument`, its conformance case is `["2026-03"]` and its golden files are named for it.

**Decisions already taken, with what lost.**

- Budget lines have a stable id; the wire keeps names and the budget document carries an optional `id`
  per line. Each budget version owns the names its month shows. Why: the stand-in joins everything by
  name, so renaming a line would silently drop its history from every total. Rejected: names as identity;
  inferring a rename from a line's position; one global name per line.
- A line id is an integer minted in the app's database, written on the wire as a decimal string like the
  other minted ids (a change's, a history step's, a subscription's); the contract's `BudgetLineDoc.id` is
  the type to match. Every minted id comes from a column declared `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, so
  an id is never reused and a stale handle can never point at a newer object.
- A transaction's line must exist in the budget in force for the transaction's own month; a line named by
  something that has no month (an establishment's default line, a pot's link, a subscription's line) is
  resolved in the current month. Every line menu says which month it is for. Why: the person decided that
  a transaction of a closed month can still be recategorised, and a line the month's budget lacks would
  count in no group of that month. Rejected: validating everything against the current month.
- The server runs read-only when no `--db` is given, and a write without a handler answers `read_only`.
  Why: the write side lands one domain at a time and the app is never half-broken. Rejected: a switch that
  flips every write at once.
- Refusals a person must be able to read are one error kind, `refused`, with a reason from a closed
  list; `bad_request` keeps meaning a bug in a client. Rejected: one kind per refusal; free text from the
  server.
- Migrations are recorded by name and every missing one is applied; names are assigned in advance, one
  owner each. This work owns `0002_budget` and no other.

**The schema: migration `0002_budget`.** Five tables. The columns are the starting point; a column this
work proves it needs may be added, in this file only.

- `lines(id, builtin)`: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`; `builtin` is 0 or 1. The migration seeds
  one row, the fees line, with `builtin = 1` and an explicit id, so the built-in line has the same id in
  every database. Not journaled: a minted id is never taken back, and undoing a save leaves its ids
  behind, unused.
- `budget_versions(from_month)`: one row per version, keyed by the month it starts in.
- `budget_version_lines(from_month, group_key, position, line_id, name, cents, flag)`: the lines of a
  version. `from_month` references `budget_versions`; `line_id` references `lines`; `group_key` is one of
  the five keys; `position` is the line's place within its group; `cents` is the amount in integer cents,
  never negative; `flag` is null when the line has none. `line_id` is unique per version and `name` is
  unique per version.
- `scenarios(name, position, doc)`: one row per saved scenario; `name` is unique; `position` gives the
  list's order; `doc` is the scenario's document.
- `closed_months(month, closed_on)`: one row per closed month, with the Brazil day it was closed on. This
  work creates the table, registers it and reads it; nothing writes it until the work that closes a month
  ({{V4}}), so here a closed month exists only in a fixture.

Every table declares its primary key, `NOT NULL` where a value is required, its foreign keys, and a
`CHECK` for every closed set of values (`group_key`, `builtin`) and for the amount that cannot be
negative. The proof includes a test in which the database itself, with no Go validation in the way,
refuses a duplicate (the same name twice in one version; the same `line_id` twice in one version), an
invalid value (a `group_key` outside the five) and a negative amount. The four tables other than `lines`
are entered in the recorder's registry; a line in a budget version and a closed month are rows that are
facts by existing (set tables), and so is a version. Which shape `scenarios` takes, and each table's key,
are the implementer's, within what the criteria observe. A version and its lines are a parent and its
children: removing a version removes its lines in the same change, and an undo brings both back.

**Which budget a month has.** A month uses the latest version that starts at or before it; a month before
the first version uses the first (`budgetFor` in `budget-versions.ts`). With no version at all a month has
no budget: the five groups, empty. What a month's budget *has* is the set of line ids of that version,
and, when that set is not empty, the fees line too.

**Saving for a month.** `budget.save(month, draft)` makes the document the budget from that month on.
`budget.applyScenario(month, draft)` is the same operation under its own method name: same rules, same
refusals, same effects. The steps, which are the stand-in's `saveFrom` with ids added:

1. A save or an apply for a closed month is refused with `month_closed` and changes nothing.
2. For every closed month later than the saved one, what was in force for it before this save stays its
   budget. Where a version already starts at that closed month it is left exactly as it is. Where none
   does, one is written there holding exactly what was in force for that month (the same line ids, names,
   amounts, flags, groups and order), read before anything else is changed. The work that closes a month
   ({{V4}}) will write a version at every month it closes, so the second case will only occur in a
   fixture; it is implemented all the same, because that is what the stand-in does and what its test
   pins.
3. Every other version that starts later than the saved month is removed.
4. The document is written as the version that starts at the saved month, replacing one that starts
   there.
5. For every closed month later than the saved one, the document is written again as the version that
   starts at the month after it, unless that month is closed too.
6. Versions that start before the saved month are not touched.

A closed month earlier than the saved one is protected only by a version that starts at or before it,
which closing will always have written; this work adds no second protection and its fixtures give an
earlier closed month a version of its own. One consequence to keep in mind for later work: a save for a
month earlier than every existing version becomes the first version, and so also the budget of every
month before it.

A save that leaves every table as it was (the document of a version that starts at the saved month, sent
back unchanged, with no later version to remove) records an empty change and answers its id, whose undo
is a no-op: the result type has no null to answer "nothing to do" with. A closed month's own version that
is kept appears in no effect.

**Ids and names.**

- A line without an `id` is new and gets one when a budget is saved or applied: one id per new line per
  save, the same in every version that save writes. Saving a scenario mints nothing.
- A line whose `id` is kept and whose name changed is a rename: the versions written by this save carry
  the new name, and earlier versions and closed months keep the name they had. Nothing else moves: the id
  is the identity, so a reorder, a change of amount, of flag or of group keeps it too.
- A line whose id the document no longer carries is removed from the versions this save writes. Its row
  in `lines` stays. Clearing it from the transactions of the months that lose it happens in the same
  change and is separate work ({{B4}}), because the transactions' tables do not exist yet ({{T1}}).
- The fees line is in no group and no document. It cannot be renamed or removed. Its name is fixed and
  the server's: "Tarifas e juros". It can be named in a write, under that name, in any month whose budget
  has at least one line.
- A line's name is stored as it was sent: trimming is only how emptiness is judged (a scenario's name, by
  contrast, is stored trimmed). Two names are the same when they are the same string, which is also what
  the schema's uniqueness enforces.
- A flag that is absent or empty is no flag, as in the stand-in's `cleanDraft`, and is answered as an
  absent field, never as null: the contract's field is optional, not nullable.
- A save can hand a name from one line to another (two lines swap names; one takes the name another had
  while that one is renamed or removed). With uniqueness enforced row by row by the database, the order
  of the writes matters in the save and again in its undo. The recorder was built with this case named
  ({{F2}}); a criterion below pins a swap and its undo.

**What a document must satisfy.** A draft being edited is not validated beyond its shape: the person is
still typing, and the two evaluations (`budget.view` with a draft, `budget.evaluateScenario`) accept an
empty or repeated name; neither is touched here. `save`, `applyScenario` and `saveScenario` validate, and
answer `refused` / `invalid_budget` when:

- a line's name is empty after trimming;
- a line's name appears twice in the whole document, in one group or across groups;
- a line's name is the fees line's;
- an `id`, where present, does not exist, or appears twice in the document. An `id` that names no line,
  whatever it looks like (`"999999"`, `"abc"`, `""`), is an id that does not exist: the same rule
  `changes.undo` applies to a change id. The fees line's own id is refused too: that line is in no
  document and cannot be renamed;
- a group's key is not one of the five.

Two things follow from the code and are not optional. First, the manifest's `EditableGroupKey` is an enum
of the five keys, and write dispatch validates arguments against the manifest before the handler runs, so
over HTTP a key outside the five is answered `bad_request` and never reaches the handler. The handler's
own check stays, tested by calling the handler below the router, because handlers are plain functions
that a later command-line client will call without HTTP. Second, a group's name and the order of the
groups in a document are ignored: the five groups always exist, in the fixed order and under the fixed
names the server owns, so a group the document leaves out is a group with no lines. A document in which
one key appears twice is a case the rules do not name; see "Left to the implementer".

`bad_request` keeps its meaning, and comes first because it is parsing: a month that does not parse
(`2026-13`), an amount that is negative or that `ParseReais` refuses, a field the schema does not know.
Then the closed month, as the stand-in's `write` calls `assertOpen` before anything else. Then the
document's validation. A refusal of any kind changes nothing and adds no row to the journal.

**The document read.** `budget.document(month)` answers the version in force for the month: the five
groups in the fixed order with the fixed names, each line with its `id`, the name that version gives it,
its amount as `Reais` and its flag when it has one, in the version's order within the group.

**Scenarios.**

- `budget.saveScenario(name, draft)` trims the name and uses "Cenário sem nome" when it is blank; the
  constant joins `internal/api/messages.go`. It answers the change id and the name it kept. A scenario
  saved under an existing name replaces it and goes to the end of the list (`budget.ts`: filter, then
  append). It validates as a save does, has no month and so no closed-month refusal, and mints nothing: a
  line without an id is stored without one.
- `budget.scenarios()` answers the saved scenarios in list order, each document with the five groups in
  the fixed order and names. A line that has an id is answered with its current name, looked up by id, so
  that applying an old scenario does not bring an old name back. "Current" is read here as everything
  that has no month is read: the name the line has in the budget in force in the current month. A line
  without an id is answered with the name it was saved with.
- The scenario editor of the interface changes amounts only, so a scenario's lines are a document's
  lines with their ids; the server does not rely on that.

**The line menu.** `transactions.filterOptions(month)` keeps answering `accounts` as today and `tags` as
today (empty; the known tags arrive with the transactions' tables ({{T1}})). `lines` becomes the menu of
the budget in force for the month asked:

- when that budget has at least one line: its lines in the stand-in's order, group by group: `var`,
  `fix`, `res`, `prov`, then the fees line, then `rec`; within a group, the version's order. Each option
  is the line's name in that version and its group's fixed name. The fees line's option is
  `{"name":"Tarifas e juros","group":"Tarifas e juros"}`, placed after the provisions whether or not that
  group has lines (`lineOptions` in `transactions.ts`);
- when it has none, or the month has no budget: an empty list, with no fees line either
  (`first-run-line-menu.test.ts`).

Options carry no id: the wire keeps names.

**The refusals this work is the first to produce**, with the sentence the interface shows for each. The
server sends only the kind and the reason; the sentences live in the interface ({{F6}}) and are quoted
here so the reasons are not confused.

| reason | when, in this work | what the person reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month_closed` | saving or applying a budget for a closed month | "Esse mês já está fechado." |
| `invalid_budget` | saving a budget or a scenario with a duplicate or empty line name, an unknown or repeated line id, an unknown group | "O budget tem linha sem nome ou repetida." |

Both leave the harness's list of reasons that have no producer. `unknown_line` ("Essa linha não existe no
budget desse mês.") is produced by later writes that name a line, not here.

**Failure paths that touch this work.**

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the migration fails | its transaction rolls back; the copy taken before it is beside the file; `serve` exits naming the path and the reason, never the content |
| the database holds a migration the binary does not know, or a changed one | refused at start; so once `0002_budget` has been applied to a database that matters, its file is never edited again |
| a write fails halfway, or waits out the five-second lock | one transaction: nothing of it is kept; the answer is `internal` |
| an undo meets a later change | `refused` / `stale_change`; nothing is restored |
| a line is renamed, reordered or removed | ids hold |
| the process stops between a save's commit and its answer | the change is stored; the interface says the result could not be confirmed and refetches |
| two tabs save at once | writes queue; each is its own change; an undo that lost the race is refused |
| the snapshot is missing | the three writes read nothing from the ledger and work; the three reads keep answering `ledger_unavailable`, as the existing test requires |

**Where this departs from the stand-in on purpose.** Each is pinned by a test, and the report of the work
names the test: line ids instead of names, with names owned by each version and group names and order
owned by the server; a line menu that follows the month asked instead of the current month's budget;
scenarios answered with current names; a closed month refused with a typed reason instead of a thrown
error; a document validated where the stand-in validates nothing; a negative amount refused where the
stand-in stores it; undo by inverse, refused when overwritten since, instead of restoring a snapshot of
the whole budget.

**Known next users, not built here,** so the design does not make them impossible: the transactions'
tables reference `lines` and show a transaction the name its line has in the budget of its own month
({{T1}}); writes that name a line resolve the name to an id in a month's budget, the fees line included,
and refuse with `unknown_line` otherwise ({{T2}}, the line writes on a transaction); a save clears the
references of the transactions whose month lost a line ({{B4}}); the budget's figures look spending up by
line id and compare a scenario by line id ({{B3}}); a pot is linked to a line ({{S2}}); closing a month
writes `closed_months` and a version of its own ({{V4}}); a save calls the rules that classify new
transactions after its commit ({{R2}}). The menu and those lookups must come from one function of "the
lines a month's budget has", so a menu never offers what a write would refuse.

**Left to the implementer** (what makes this bead `spec:open`), each with what constrains it:

- the id the migration gives the fees line, and each table's key and exact declarations beyond the
  constraints above: the id is fixed by the migration and the same in every database;
- how `scenarios.doc` is written: deterministic bytes for the same scenario (it appears in the golden
  effects), amounts as integer cents, ids kept, no float;
- where the version arithmetic of a save lives. Only `internal/authored` executes SQL against the app's
  database, and it may import only `internal/money` and `internal/brday`; a "month after" belongs in
  `internal/brday` if it is needed outside `internal/api`;
- what a document with the same group key twice does: either every line is kept, in document order, or
  the save is refused with `invalid_budget`. No line may be dropped silently, the choice is the same for
  the three writes, and a test pins it;
- the name answered for a scenario's line whose id the current month's budget does not have: the answer
  must validate (a name is required), be deterministic, and keep the id; the name the scenario was saved
  with is the one source left;
- what an undo answers when it cannot restore a name because a later save gave that name to another
  line: that is the undo engine's rule ({{F2}}), `stale_change` or `internal`. What is fixed here is that
  it does not succeed and changes nothing.

**Privacy and conventions.** Nothing here needs a real ledger. A real ledger is a person's whole financial
history and this repository is public: fixtures are invented, and no value from a real snapshot (an
amount, a description, a name, a document, an id) is ever printed, logged or copied into a file, a
commit, a bead or a pull request. Work in your own git worktree, on your own branch, and stop at local
commits: atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a
plan in a commit message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path; a test
already forbids floats in `internal/api` and covers `internal/authored`. Every SQL statement over the
app's database is a registered constant. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is
English; the Portuguese this work adds is the scenario's default name, in `messages.go`. A design value
in a component comes from a token; this work touches no component. New files in `internal/api` log
nothing: the request log holds the verb, the route, the status, the duration and the error kind, never an
argument, a body or a line's name.

## Acceptance criteria
The examples use one invented budget, B0: `rec` Salário 10000 and Renda extra 1500 with the flag
"Não garantida"; `fix` Contas da casa 2000 and Saúde 500; `var` Mercado 400 and Delivery 200; `prov`
Remédios 150; `res` Viagens 600. The invented ledgers run on a clock fixed at 2026-03-20, so the current
month is 2026-03.

Schema
- [ ] A database that held only the journal's tables gains the five tables when opened; the migration is
recorded once under the name `0002_budget`; opening it again applies nothing and seeds nothing twice.
- [ ] `lines` holds exactly one row with `builtin = 1` after migration, and two databases created
independently give it the same id.
- [ ] From a test, directly against the migrated schema, the database refuses: a second line with the
same name in one version; the same `line_id` twice in one version; a `group_key` of `xyz`; a line of -1
cents; a line whose `line_id` is not in `lines`; a line whose version does not exist.
- [ ] Every statement this work adds is a registered constant and is prepared by the existing test; the
four tables other than `lines` are in the recorder's registry and `lines` is written only by the
statement that mints an id.

Versions (each starts from B0 saved as the only version, from 2026-02, with no closed month unless said)
- [ ] `budget.document` for 2026-02, 2026-03 and 2026-01 answers B0: a month before the first version
uses the first.
- [ ] Saving for 2026-03 with Saúde at 900: the documents of 2026-03 and 2026-04 answer 900.00 and those
of 2026-02 and 2026-01 answer 500.00.
- [ ] Saving for 2026-04 with Saúde at 700: 2026-03 answers 500.00 and 2026-04 answers 700.00; a save
for 2026-03 with 900 after it makes 2026-04 answer 900.00, and `budget_versions` then holds exactly
2026-02 and 2026-03.
- [ ] With 2026-04 closed and no version starting there: saving for 2026-03 with 900 makes 2026-03 answer
900.00, 2026-04 answer 500.00 and 2026-05 answer 900.00, and `budget_versions` holds 2026-02, 2026-03,
2026-04 and 2026-05.
- [ ] With 2026-04 and 2026-05 closed: after the same save 2026-04 and 2026-05 answer 500.00 and 2026-06
answers 900.00.
- [ ] With 2026-04 closed and holding a version of its own in which Saúde is 650: after the same save
2026-04 still answers 650.00 and the change has no effect on any row of that version.
- [ ] With 2026-03 closed: `budget.save` and `budget.applyScenario` for 2026-03 each answer 409
`{"error":{"kind":"refused","reason":"month_closed"}}`; the canonical dump of the journaled tables and
the row counts of `changes`, `change_effects` and `lines` are what they were. The same holds when the
document sent is also invalid: the closed month is what is answered.
- [ ] With B0 saved as the only version from 2026-03: a save for 2026-01 leaves `budget_versions` holding
exactly 2026-01, and the documents of 2025-12 and 2026-03 both answer what was saved.
- [ ] Saving for 2026-02 the document just read for 2026-02, unchanged, answers a change id whose change
has no effect, and undoing it answers success and changes nothing.

Ids and names
- [ ] B0 saved without ids is answered with an id on each of its 8 lines: 8 distinct decimal strings,
none of them the fees line's id; a second `budget.document` answers the same ids.
- [ ] Renaming Mercado to Feira (same id) in a save for 2026-03: the document of 2026-03 answers that id
under "Feira" and the document of 2026-02 answers the same id under "Mercado". With 2026-04 closed, the
document of 2026-04 answers it under "Mercado" and that of 2026-05 under "Feira".
- [ ] Reversing the lines of `fix` and appending a new line "Nova linha" of 10 answers that group in
exactly the draft's order; each existing line keeps its id, and the new line's id is greater than every
id minted before it.
- [ ] A new line that a save writes into two versions (the saved month and the month after a later closed
month) has one and the same id in both.
- [ ] After removing Delivery in one save and adding a line in the next, the added line's id is not the
one Delivery had; after undoing a save that minted ids, `lines` still holds them and the next save mints
greater ones.
- [ ] A document that carries Saúde's id on a line of `var` moves the line to that group under the same
id.
- [ ] A save in which Mercado and Delivery swap names (ids kept) succeeds, the document answers each id
under the other's name, and undoing it restores both.
- [ ] A line whose flag is `""` is answered without a `flag` field; Renda extra is answered with
`"flag":"Não garantida"`.
- [ ] An amount sent as `10.005` is answered `10.01`, and one sent as `1e3` is answered `1000.00`.

Validation (each for `budget.save`, `budget.applyScenario` and `budget.saveScenario`)
- [ ] 409 `refused` / `invalid_budget`, with nothing changed and no row added to the journal, for: a line
named `""`; a line named with three spaces; two lines named "Mercado" in `var`; "Mercado" in `var` and in
`fix`; a line named "Tarifas e juros"; an id of `"999999"`; an id of `"abc"`; the same id on two lines;
the fees line's id on a line.
- [ ] 400 `bad_request`, with nothing changed, for: an amount of -1; an amount of 2000000000; a group key
of `xyz`; a line with a field the contract does not have; and, where the method takes a month, the month
`2026-13`.
- [ ] Called below the router, the handler of each of the three writes answers the `invalid_budget`
refusal for a group key of `xyz`.
- [ ] A document that leaves out the `res` group is saved, and the document read back has `res` with no
lines; a document whose groups are in another order and carry other names is read back in the fixed
order with the fixed names.
- [ ] A document in which `var` appears twice behaves as the implementer chose and as a test pins:
either all its lines are kept in document order, or the write is refused with `invalid_budget`; in
neither case is a line missing from a successful save.

Scenarios
- [ ] On a database with no scenario `budget.scenarios` answers `[]`.
- [ ] `budget.saveScenario("  ", draft)` answers `"name":"Cenário sem nome"` and a decimal change id, and
`budget.scenarios` then lists one scenario of that name; `saveScenario("  Sem extra ", draft)` keeps it as
"Sem extra".
- [ ] After saving "A", "B", "C" and then "A" again with another document, `budget.scenarios` answers B,
C, A, and A holds the second document; undoing that last save answers A, B, C with A's first document.
- [ ] A scenario saved with one line that has no id is answered with that line still without an id, and
the row count of `lines` did not change.
- [ ] A scenario saved with Mercado's id, after a save for 2026-03 renames that id to "Feira", is answered
with that line named "Feira".
- [ ] `budget.applyScenario` passes every criterion under Versions and under Ids and names that `save`
passes (one table of cases run over both methods), and the method recorded on its change is
`budget.applyScenario`.

The line menu
- [ ] On a database with no version, `transactions.filterOptions` answers `"lines":[]` for 2026-03.
- [ ] After a save of five empty groups, it answers `"lines":[]`: no fees line.
- [ ] With B0 as the only version, from 2026-03, the menu of 2026-03 is exactly, in order: Mercado and
Delivery (group "Variáveis"), Contas da casa and Saúde ("Fixos e essenciais"), Viagens ("Reservas de
desejo"), Remédios ("Provisões"), Tarifas e juros ("Tarifas e juros"), Salário and Renda extra
("Receita"); the menu of 2026-01 is the same list.
- [ ] With a budget whose only line is Salário, the menu is
`[{"name":"Tarifas e juros","group":"Tarifas e juros"},{"name":"Salário","group":"Receita"}]`.
- [ ] After a save for 2026-04 that renames Mercado to Feira, the menu of 2026-03 offers "Mercado" and
that of 2026-04 offers "Feira".
- [ ] `accounts` and `tags` of the answer are what they were before this work, over both invented ledgers.

Journal, undo and the harness
- [ ] Each of the three writes is one change with author `person` and its own qualified method name; its
effects name only `budget_versions`, `budget_version_lines` and `scenarios`, never `lines`; undoing it
returns the canonical dump of every journaled table to the dump taken before the write.
- [ ] After a save S1 renames Mercado to Feira and a later save S2 for the same month adds a new line
named "Mercado", undoing S1 does not succeed: it answers `refused` / `stale_change` or `internal`, and
the canonical dump is the one taken before the attempt.
- [ ] The write conformance harness has a case, in the mode of a recorded change, for each of the three
writes, with its golden effects file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`; a refusal case for
`month_closed` and one for `invalid_budget`; both reasons are gone from the list of reasons without a
producer, and the three methods are gone from `writesWithoutHandler`.
- [ ] `authoredReadCases` holds at least: `budget.document` for two months whose versions name one line
differently, `budget.scenarios`, and `transactions.filterOptions` for the same two months, each with its
golden file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`; none of them is written in the shape the
interface's equality test scans for.
- [ ] No file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/` or `empty/` changes (`git diff --stat` over the
branch shows none), and `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts` passes untouched.
- [ ] On a server without the app's database: `budget.document`, `budget.scenarios` and
`transactions.filterOptions` answer byte for byte what they answered before, the three writes answer 403
`read_only`, and `internal/api/budget_test.go`'s existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Over a snapshot that cannot be read the three reads answer 503 `ledger_unavailable`; with the
snapshot file missing, `budget.save` succeeds.
- [ ] The test that proves no handler logs what it reads passes over the new cases, with the line names
and scenario names of those cases among the strings it looks for.
- [ ] `budget.view` with a draft still answers `read_only` and `budget.evaluateScenario` still answers
`read_only`: neither gained a handler here.

Proof of the proofs
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against a deliberate break named in the report of the
work: later versions left in place by a save; the document resumed into a month that is closed; a kept
closed month's version overwritten; a new line minted once per version instead of once per save; a rename
stored under a new id; the closed-month check removed; each of the five validations removed in turn; the
menu made to ignore its month; the fees line offered by a budget with no line; the menu's group order
changed; a scenario replaced in place instead of moved to the end; a scenario's names answered as saved
instead of looked up; one of the schema's `CHECK`s and one of its uniqueness rules dropped.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, a budget saved over HTTP on a server started with `--db` is
answered by `budget.document` after the process restarts with the same ids, and every criterion above has
a test that was seen to fail against its break.

## Tests
- Unit, over a temporary migrated database (`internal/authored`): the schema's refusals of a duplicate,
an invalid value, a negative amount and a broken reference, with no Go validation in the way.
- Table, over invented authored states built with `authoredtest` (`internal/authored`): the version in
force for a month (before the first version, between two, after the last, no version); the save's version
arithmetic for every case under Versions, ported from the group "versioning by month" of
`web/src/api/fake/budget.test.ts` with its months moved to the fixture's clock, plus the cases the
stand-in does not have (two closed months in a row, a closed month with a version of its own, a save
earlier than every version).
- Table (`internal/authored` or `internal/api`, where the validation lives): every row of the two
validation criteria, over the three writes.
- Unit: minting (once per new line per save, never reused, not undone), rename, reorder, move between
groups, the swap of two names and its undo.
- Table, ported from the group "scenarios" of `budget.test.ts` (the cases of `saveScenario`,
`scenarios` and `applyScenario`; the cases of `evaluateScenario` are not this work's): the default name,
the trimmed name, replacement and its place in the list, undo, names looked up by id.
- Table, ported from `web/src/api/fake/transactions.test.ts` and `first-run-line-menu.test.ts`: the menu
of no budget, of a budget with no line, of a first budget, of a month before the first version, of two
versions that name a line differently, and of a budget with one income line.
- Conformance, writes (`internal/api`, the harness's lists): a recorded-change case per write with golden
effects and the undo that returns the dump; a refusal case per reason first produced here.
- Conformance and golden, reads, third state (`internal/api`, `authoredReadCases`): the document, the
scenarios and the menu over the full invented ledger with an invented authored state that holds two
versions, a renamed line, a flag, a scenario and all five groups.
- Integration with `httptest` over a router built on both stores: the status and body of each refusal;
`bad_request` for what the manifest's schema refuses; `read_only` without the database; the answer after
the database is closed and opened again.
- The existing tests that pin a server without the database, unchanged, and the gate once at the end. The
review breaks each new guard once more before the work is accepted.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/authored/migrations/`, `internal/authored/`, `internal/authored/authoredtest/`,
`internal/api/budget.go`, `internal/api/budget_writes.go`, `internal/api/transactions.go`,
`internal/api/messages.go`, `internal/brday/brday.go`, `internal/brday/brday_test.go`,
`internal/api/budget_test.go`, `internal/api/budget_writes_test.go`, `internal/api/transactions_test.go`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/fake/budget.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/budget-versions.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/budget.test.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/transactions.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/transactions.test.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/first-run-data.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/first-run-line-menu.test.ts`, `web/src/api/contract/budget.ts`,
`web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`, `internal/contract/contract.json`, `internal/api/budget_view.go`,
`internal/api/fresh_install.go`, `internal/api/net_worth_chart.go`,
`internal/api/unreadable_snapshot_test.go`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/empty/`, `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`,
`web/src/screens/budget/BudgetScreen.vue`, `bin/ci`

One migration; in `internal/authored`, the budget's store (one or two new files), its entries in the
recorder's registry and in the statement registry, and the reads it adds to the authored view; one new
builder file in `authoredtest`; in `internal/api`, two read handlers and the line menu changed in place,
one new file for the three write handlers, one constant, and the registration of the handlers wherever
write dispatch placed it; at most one function in `internal/brday`. The test files that hold the
harness's lists (`writesWithoutHandler`, the reasons without a producer, the write cases and
`authoredReadCases`) are edited where the harness put them. That is about twelve code files in three
packages, which is why a split is proposed on the first line. The contract, the manifest, the interface
and the stand-in are read, not changed: the contract's part of this was done before
({{B1}}). `budget.view`, `budget.establishments`, `budget.evaluateScenario`, the shell's closed months and
every transaction read are left alone.

## Recovery path
The migration only adds tables and seeds one row. If it fails, its transaction rolls back and the server
exits; when the database already held data, the copy the migration runner took before migrating is beside
it (`<name>.before-<UTC timestamp>`). To go back: stop the server; check the copy (`PRAGMA
integrity_check`, the application id); put it in place of the database with no `-wal` or `-shm` file
beside it; start a binary that does not carry this migration, since a database that holds a migration the
binary does not know is refused at start. A budget saved by mistake is not a recovery case: the save's
change id undoes it. Once the migration has been applied to a database that matters its file is frozen;
a correction is a new migration, never an edit.

title: Build the conformance harness for writes, the invented authored states and their golden directories
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing on screen changes with this piece. What it makes possible is that every action that will save
something (a budget, a category, a tag, a note) arrives already proved in three ways: that it saves what
it says and nothing else, that taking it back restores exactly what was there before, and that nothing
the person typed ends up in the server's logs. Without it each of those would be checked by hand, action
by action, or not at all. If this piece were wrong the person would be the one to find out, weeks later:
an undo that leaves a stray tag behind, an answer of "nothing to do" that did change something, a
budget line's name sitting in a log file.

## Outcome
`internal/api` has a conformance harness for writes beside the one for reads. Every write and evaluation
is of exactly one of five modes, each mode has its check, and a test requires a case in its mode for
every method that has a handler. A new package, `internal/authored/authoredtest`, builds invented states
of the app's database for tests, as `internal/ledger/ledgertest` builds invented snapshots. Read
conformance gains a third state, the full invented ledger with an invented authored state, with a list
of cases of a type of its own and its own golden directory; the interface's equality test checks that
it leaves that list out. `TestEveryGoldenFileHasACase` knows both new directories, and the test that
proves no handler logs what it reads runs every write case too. The harness is proved by breaking an
undo on purpose and watching it fail.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is the SQLite snapshot a
separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app only reads it. *The app's database* is
`finwise.db`, owned by the package `internal/authored`, where everything the person authors is kept; the
server has one only when started with `--db`. *The manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, the
generated description of the API's 82 methods with a schema for each method's arguments and result and
one for the error envelope; 55 methods are of class `write` and one, `budget.evaluateScenario`, of class
`evaluate`. *The recorder* is the layer of `internal/authored` through which every change to the app's
database is written; *the journal* is what it writes, the tables `changes` (one row per change: author,
method, instant, Brazil day, whether it was extended or undone) and `change_effects` (one row per effect:
`change_id, seq, tbl, key, col, before, after`); a *journaled table* is one the recorder knows from its
closed registry, in one of two shapes (one row of independent columns per key, where an effect is one
column changing; or rows that are facts by existing, where an effect is one row appearing or
disappearing). *Undo* is the inverse of a change's recorded effects, refused with `refused` /
`stale_change` when a later change still in force touched what it would restore. *The stand-in* is the
in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on. A *golden file* is
the exact, committed answer of one call over an invented fixture.

Write dispatch is delivered by {{F4c}}: the router runs a handler for a write inside one transaction,
through a recorder that writes the change's row only with its first effect or when the handler asks for
the id it must answer, and commits it; it answers `read_only` when the server has no database or the
method no handler, and `refused` with a reason from a closed list of nine (`month_closed`,
`future_month`, `pending_reviews`, `stale_change`, `not_found`, `unknown_line`, `invalid_budget`,
`unstable_pot`, `split_with_reimbursement`); and it has `changes.undo` as its first and, when this slice
starts, only write handler.

**What the code is today (each point checked in the file named).**

- `internal/api/conformance_test.go`: a `readCase` is a method and its arguments as the JSON array a
  client posts. `readCases` holds a base list, and the test files of each domain append to it in an
  `init` (`budget_test.go`, `accounts_test.go`, `pots_test.go`, `transactions_test.go` and others).
  `TestEveryRegisteredReadHasAConformanceCase` requires a case for every registered read and a handler
  for every case. `TestEveryAnswerValidatesAgainstItsResultSchema` answers every case over the two
  invented ledgers and validates the body with `conformanceProblem`, which compiles each method's result
  schema from the manifest (draft 7, `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6`).
  `TestTheConformanceCheckRejectsAnAnswerThatDoesNotMatch` feeds the check five broken answers and
  requires it to refuse each: that is the house pattern for a check that must be able to fail.
- `internal/api/golden_test.go`: `TestEveryAnswerMatchesItsGoldenFile` compares each answer,
  pretty-printed, with `testdata/golden/<ledger>/<name>` for the ledgers `full` and `empty`. `goldenName`
  derives the file name from the call: `<domain>.<method>.json`, or `<domain>.<method>.<slug>.json`
  where the slug is the argument array as compact JSON with sorted keys, lowercased, every run outside
  `a-z0-9` turned into one `-`. `-update` rewrites the files and `goldenUpdateRefusal` refuses it while
  `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set. `TestEveryGoldenFileHasACase` globs `testdata/golden/*/*.json` and
  fails on any file that is not a read case over `full` or `empty`, so today a file in any other
  directory fails it. `full/` and `empty/` hold 59 files each. `testdata/golden/README.md` documents the
  two directories, the naming and the update command.
- `internal/api/harness_test.go` and `fixtures_test.go`: `newReadEnv` builds a router over a fixture
  ledger with a session open; `ledgerNamed` knows `full` (`newFullLedger`: every shape the rules know)
  and `empty`; `fixtureNow` is the server's clock in those ledgers, noon of 20 March 2026 in Brazil.
- `internal/api/handler_silence_test.go`: `TestOnlyTheRequestLogWritesAnything` allows only `logging.go`
  and `router.go` to name a logging package. `TestNoHandlerLogsWhatItReads` runs every read case over
  both ledgers with the default `slog` logger, the standard `log` output and the request log captured,
  and fails if any of them holds one of a list of strings only the fixtures and the arguments hold
  (`tx-`, `acc-`, `card-itau`, `LIVRARIA`, `EXEMPLO`, `Exemplo`, `2026-02`, `no-such`, `12345678`), or
  if the two default loggers received a single byte.
- `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`: the interface's equality test. It compares, call by call, the
  backend's golden files of `empty/` with what the stand-in answers over an empty ledger. It finds the
  calls by their written shape in the Go sources: `recordedCalls` scans every `_test.go` file of
  `internal/api` for the literal ``readCase{"domain.method", `[...]`}`` anywhere, and for the bare
  entries ``{"domain.method", `[...]`},`` inside `var readCases = []readCase{ ... }`. Every call it
  finds must have a golden file in `empty/`, and every file of `empty/` must be found.
  `web/src/test/replay.ts` reads only the directories `full` and `empty` (`RECORDED_LEDGERS`).

**1. `internal/authored/authoredtest`.** It builds an invented `finwise.db` for a test: created in the
test's temporary directory, migrated, with the clock handed in, so that everything the database derives
from the clock is deterministic. The instant of creation is a parameter, because the *tracking start
month* (the month the database was created in, from which the app asks about uncategorised
transactions) is set from it once and never again. When this lands the only content a database can have
is the journal's own tables and that month; each later slice adds the builders for the tables it owns,
as `ledgertest` has one builder per kind of row. A builder is constrained by the two guards of
`internal/authored`: every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant, and a
statement that inserts, updates or deletes in an authored table outside the recorder fails a test. So a
builder goes through the package's own functions and the recorder and must not need an exemption from
either guard.

**2. The canonical dump.** A deterministic text of the content of every journaled table, taken from the
recorder's registry so that a table a later slice adds is dumped without anyone editing the harness. It
is JSON, with the tables in name order and each table's rows in key order; its exact shape is the
implementer's as long as it is deterministic and reads well in a diff. Two databases in the same state
give the same bytes; one column or one row of difference gives different bytes. The recorder's package
is expected to carry such a dump already for its own property test (the recorder, the journal and the
undo engine are {{F2}}'s): the harness uses that one, and if what is there does not meet the rule above,
bringing it to the rule is part of this slice and the one change it makes inside `internal/authored`.

**3. Write conformance, by mode.** Every write and evaluation is of exactly one mode, and a test
requires a case for each handler in its mode:

- *a recorded change*: the answer validates against the method's result schema in the manifest; its
  effects match a golden file under `testdata/golden/writes/`; undoing it returns the canonical dump of
  every journaled table to the dump taken before the write;
- *nothing to do* (a null answer): no row is added to the journal;
- *an evaluation*: no table changes at all;
- *an extension of an earlier change* (`transactions.applyLineToEstablishment`, "all purchases here",
  which appends its effects to the change that set the line and answers that change's id): undoing it
  returns the dump taken before its origin;
- `changes.undo` and `session.changePin`: their own tests, outside the harness. The harness names the
  two as exempt, explicitly, so that a third method cannot hide beside them.

A case states which of these it expects. A method whose mode is a recorded change may have further cases
that expect a null answer (an unknown target, or nothing to do, where the contract's result allows
null); each is checked by the rule of what it expects. A few methods answer only null until the thing
they act on has a producer, and nothing to do is their mode. The coverage test fails for a registered
write or evaluation with no case in its mode and for a case that names a method with no handler.

The write side also owes one refusal case per reason of the closed list. A refusal case expects 409
`refused` with a named reason; its body validates against the manifest's `error` schema; no table
changes at all. A test compares the reasons that have a case with the nine. Only `stale_change` has a
producer when this lands (`changes.undo` on a change it does not know), so the eight others are named in
an explicit list in the test file, in the same way the manifest walk names the writes that have no
handler yet; each slice that first produces a reason removes it from the list, and the test fails for a
reason that is in the list and has a case, or in neither.

Each check is a function that names what is wrong, as `conformanceProblem` and `readCoverageProblems`
are, so that a test can feed it a broken input and require it to complain. How a case is written in Go
(its method, its arguments, the invented ledger and the invented authored state it starts from, what it
expects, a refusal's reason) and how "no table changes at all" is observed are the implementer's, with
two constraints: the second must cover the tables that are not journaled too (`changes`,
`change_effects`, `meta` and, later, the index of transactions the database keeps), and the harness
carries no SQL that the statement rule of `internal/authored` forbids.

**4. The effects file.** A recorded-change case has one golden file,
`testdata/golden/writes/<domain>.<method>[.<slug>].json`, with the slug derived from the argument array
by the rule the read files already use (`goldenName`). It holds the answer and the change's effects in
the journal's order (by `seq`), each with its table, key, column, before and after as the recorder
writes them. Because the name comes from the call alone, two recorded-change cases of one method must
differ in their arguments, and a test fails when two cases name the same file. A file must not change
when another case is added, removed or reordered, so each case starts from a state of its own: ids
minted by the app's database are integers written as decimal strings and are deterministic, which is
what makes a change id in an answer stable. `-update` writes these files and is refused while
`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set, through `goldenUpdateRefusal`.

**5. Proving the harness when nothing real is journaled yet.** No table of the real schema is journaled
when this lands: the first ones arrive with the budget's tables ({{B2}}: the budget document, its save
and its scenarios), and the first real extension with the line writes ({{T2}}: setting a line and
applying it to the rest of an establishment). So the real list of write cases starts with what
`changes.undo` needs, and the harness proves itself over handlers registered only in tests, writing
through the recorder to scratch tables of both shapes, as the recorder's own property test and the tests
of the write dispatch do; `testdata/golden/writes/` gets its first file with the first real recorded
write, and the effects comparison is proved here on content the test holds. The proof this slice owes: a
deliberately broken undo fails it. The check that compares the dump after the undo with the dump before
the write is run against an undo made wrong on purpose (one that restores every unit but one, one that
restores a different value, one that leaves a child row behind) and must report each; the extension's
check is run against an undo that returns to the state after the origin instead of before it.

**6. The third read state.** Read conformance gains a third state: the full invented ledger together
with an invented authored state, in `testdata/golden/full-authored/`. Its cases are a list of their own,
`authoredReadCases`, of a type and a constructor of their own, because the interface's equality test
finds the cases of `readCases` by their written shape and requires a golden file in `empty/` for each.
That test gains a check that it leaves the new list out: it fails if a call of `authoredReadCases` is
ever picked up by `recordedCalls`. The authored cases are answered over a router built on both stores,
validated against the result schema and compared with their golden files, with the same `-update` and
the same refusal while `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set. The list is seeded with at least one call, so
the directory exists and the comparison can be seen failing; which call is the implementer's. No read
consults the authored store yet, so that first file equals its twin in `full/`; the reads that merge
what the person authored arrive with the slices that own them, the first being the transaction list,
detail and filter options ({{T1}}).

**7. The golden directories.** `TestEveryGoldenFileHasACase` learns both new directories, `writes/` and
`full-authored/`: a file in either that belongs to no case fails, as a stray file in `full/` or `empty/`
does today, and a file in a directory it does not know still fails. The README of the golden directory
documents the four directories, how the name of a file in each is derived from its case, and the command
that updates each. This slice changes no file of `full/` or `empty/`. The standing rule for the slices
around it, so that a diff there is never a surprise: the files of `empty/` change in one way only, the
line menu's file being renamed for its month argument ({{B1}}: the month of the line menu in the
contract). Those of `full/` change with that rename and where an answer is derived from the ledger
alone, and each such difference is read in review. Five are expected: the reimbursement candidates of a
transaction's detail ({{T5}}: reimbursements and their candidates over the whole ledger), the
establishments and people of the settings overview ({{S3}}), the subscription candidates ({{SB1}}:
subscriptions created by hand), the pots list's third group when a pot is there ({{S2}}: a pot's bucket
and its linked lines), and the card bill of a past month in the closing view ({{V3}}). The shared
invented ledger has no payroll credit, so the payday's balance and difference are proved on a ledger
built for that test ({{V5}}: the payday's transfers), not in these directories.

**8. Nothing leaks.** The test that runs every read case to prove nothing reaches the logs runs every
write case and every authored read case too, over the same three sinks. Its list of strings gains what
only the write cases and the invented authored state hold: every argument of a write case that is text
the person would have typed or that names a row (a line's name, a tag, a note, a nickname, an
establishment key) is in the list or contains a listed string. An establishment key is the identity of
an establishment or a person, with the prefix `doc:`, `name:` or `text:`, and under `doc:` it can be a
document number, which is why it is never logged and why a fixture's document number is invented.
Logging rules are unchanged: the request log holds the verb, the route, the status, the duration and the
error kind, never an argument, a body or a key, and no file of `internal/api` but `logging.go` and
`router.go` names a logging package.

**The trap in the interface's equality test.** `recordedCalls` matches the literal
``readCase{"domain.method", `[...]`}`` in any `_test.go` file of `internal/api`, not only the entries of
`readCases`. An authored read case or a write case spelled that way would be taken for a read over the
empty ledger, and `npm --prefix web test` would then ask for a golden file in `empty/` that must not
exist. That is why the new lists have a type and a constructor of their own, which the two expressions
do not match (the match is case-sensitive, so a type name ending in `ReadCase` is safe and one ending in
`readCase` is not). Only the gate shows a mistake here: `go test ./...` stays green while the web test
fails. A call that `readCases` already holds hides the mistake, because its file in `empty/` exists, so
the break that proves the new check uses a call no read case makes.

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. Golden
files are committed, so the rule applies in full: a real snapshot may be opened read-only; no value from
it (amount, description, name, document, id) is ever printed, logged, copied into a file, a commit, a
bead or a pull request; a count may be shown to the person running a test and goes into no file; a test
that touches a real ledger runs only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file. Nothing in this slice
needs a real ledger. Every fixture, of the ledger and of the app's database, is invented, and every
`-update` of the new directories refuses to run while `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set.

**Conventions.** Work happens in a git worktree of its own and ends at local commits: atomic,
Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit
message. Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path. Every SQL statement over the
app's database is a registered constant. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and everything else is
English; a design value in a component comes from a token (this slice touches no component).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `authoredtest` builds a migrated `finwise.db` in the test's temporary directory from a clock
handed in; two databases built the same way have equal canonical dumps, and one built at an instant in
another month has another tracking start month.
- [ ] The canonical dump is JSON, lists every journaled table of the recorder's registry in name order
with each table's rows in key order; a test shows equal bytes for two equal states and different bytes
after one column changes and after one row appears.
- [ ] Over test handlers on scratch tables of both shapes, a recorded-change case passes: its answer
validates against the method's result schema, its answer and effects equal its golden content, and the
dump after `changes.undo` equals the dump before the write.
- [ ] The same check fails, naming the problem, for each of three undos broken on purpose: one unit not
restored, one unit restored to a different value, one child row left behind.
- [ ] The recorded-change check fails for an answer that does not validate and for effects that differ
from the golden content by one column or by their order.
- [ ] An extension case passes: a test handler extends an earlier change, answers that change's id and
adds no row to `changes`, and the dump after undoing that id equals the dump taken before the origin;
the check fails for an undo that returns to the state after the origin.
- [ ] The nothing-to-do check passes for a handler that answers null and records nothing, and fails for
one that answers null after a row was added to `changes`.
- [ ] The evaluation check passes for a handler that stores nothing and fails for one that changes any
table, a table that is not journaled included.
- [ ] A refusal case passes for `changes.undo` on an unknown change (409, `stale_change`, body valid
against the manifest's `error` schema, no table changed), and the refusal check fails for a refusal that
left a row behind.
- [ ] The coverage test fails for a registered write or evaluation with no case in its mode, and for a
case naming a method with no handler; `changes.undo` and `session.changePin` are the only two methods
named as exempt.
- [ ] The reasons test accounts for all nine: `stale_change` by a case, the eight others by the explicit
list; it fails when a reason is in neither and when one is in both.
- [ ] The file of a recorded-change case is `testdata/golden/writes/<domain>.<method>[.<slug>].json` by
the rule of `goldenName`, and a test fails when two cases name the same file.
- [ ] `authoredReadCases` has a type and a constructor of its own and at least one case; it is answered
over the full invented ledger and an invented authored state, validates against its result schema and
equals its file in `testdata/golden/full-authored/`.
- [ ] `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts` has a check that no call of `authoredReadCases` is among the
calls it collects; the check was seen failing once, with an authored case that makes a call no entry of
`readCases` makes spelled as a `readCase{...}` literal; `npm --prefix web test` passes.
- [ ] `TestEveryGoldenFileHasACase` fails for a stray `.json` file placed in each of `full/`, `empty/`,
`full-authored/` and `writes/`, and for one in a directory of any other name.
- [ ] No commit of this slice changes a file under `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/` or
`internal/api/testdata/golden/empty/`.
- [ ] An update of the files of `writes/` or of `full-authored/` is refused while
`FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set: a test shows it.
- [ ] The no-leak test runs every write case and every authored read case, and fails when a test handler
is made to log one of its arguments through the default `slog` logger and through the standard `log`.
- [ ] `internal/api/testdata/golden/README.md` describes the four directories, the naming of a file in
each and the update command of each.
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against its own deliberate break, named in the final
report: the breaks listed in the criteria above, plus the dump against a registry entry left out of it.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, a deliberately broken undo fails the harness in a test
that stays in the suite, and no file of `full/` or `empty/` was changed by this slice.

## Tests
- Unit (`internal/authored/authoredtest`): a built database is migrated and deterministic; the creation
  instant decides the tracking start month.
- Unit: the canonical dump, equal for equal states and different for one column and for one row, over
  scratch tables of both shapes.
- Conformance, over the full invented ledger of `fixtures_test.go` and a database built by
  `authoredtest`, with handlers registered only in the test and writing to scratch tables: one case per
  mode (a recorded change, nothing to do, an evaluation, an extension) and one refusal case.
- Unit, in the pattern of `TestTheConformanceCheckRejectsAnAnswerThatDoesNotMatch`: each check fed its
  broken inputs (three broken undos, an extension undone to the wrong state, a non-conforming answer,
  changed and reordered effects, a journal row after a null answer, a table changed by an evaluation, a
  row left by a refusal).
- Unit: the coverage test, the reasons test and the test that two cases do not share a file, each with
  a test of the test, in the pattern of `TestTheCoverageCheckFailsWhenAHandlerIsMissingOrInvented`.
- Golden: the seeded authored read case in `full-authored/`; the 59 files of each of `full/` and `empty/`
  untouched by this slice.
- Unit: `TestEveryGoldenFileHasACase` over the four directories; the update refusal for the new ones.
- Unit: the no-leak test over write cases and authored read cases, with a handler that logs.
- Unit (vitest, `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`), over the Go test sources, the golden files of
  `empty/` and the stand-in's empty ledger: the new check that the authored list is left out, and the
  existing equality still holding.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/authored/authoredtest/`, `internal/api/conformance_test.go`,
`internal/api/golden_test.go`, `internal/api/handler_silence_test.go`, `internal/api/harness_test.go`,
`internal/api/fixtures_test.go`, `internal/api/write_conformance_test.go`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/README.md`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/`, `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`
**Reads only:** `internal/authored/`, `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/empty/`, `internal/api/reads_coverage_test.go`,
`internal/api/router_test.go`, `internal/contract/contract.json`, `internal/ledger/ledgertest/`,
`web/src/test/replay.ts`, `bin/ci`

Test code and one test-support package: about ten files, in `internal/api`'s tests, the new
`authoredtest` and one test of the interface that gains one check; no production file of `internal/api`
and no screen. It stays one bead although it reaches three places, because its parts share
`golden_test.go` and the README, and because `authoredtest` has no user but this harness when it lands.
`write_conformance_test.go` is new and may be split in two if the cases and the checks read better
apart. `internal/authored` is used as delivered; the one change this slice may make there is bringing
the canonical dump to the rule of point 2. The golden files of `full/` and `empty/` are read and not
changed; `testdata/golden/writes/` gains its first file only with the first real recorded write, which
belongs to a later slice, so the directory may not exist in the tree when this lands.

It is labelled critical although it changes no production code: every later write is accepted on this
harness's word, so a check here that cannot fail lets a wrong undo through in silence. Only `bin/ci`
proves it whole, because a mistake in how a Go case is spelled is caught by a test of the interface.

title: Let the interface talk to a real backend
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the interface can only run on the invented dataset bundled with it. After this lands the same interface, built for real use, talks to the backend: the PIN is checked by the server, the screens show what the server answers, and three things that used to fail silently now say something. Trying to change anything shows one message that the app is read-only for now and leaves the screen as it was. A session that expired brings back the PIN screen. A request that fails shows a message with a button to try again instead of a blank page.

## Outcome
An HTTP implementation of the interface's API contract beside the in-memory stand-in, chosen when the interface is built, and one place that turns every failure of the API into what the person sees.

## Context
finwise's interface reaches its backend through one TypeScript interface, `FinwiseApi` (`web/src/api/types.ts`). `web/src/main.ts` provides an implementation with `app.provide(apiKey, createFakeApi())`, and everything else calls `useApi()` (`web/src/api/context.ts`). The only implementation is the in-memory stand-in under `web/src/api/fake/`, which serves the design prototype's dataset; the parity check that measures every screen against the design depends on that dataset.

A generated manifest, `internal/contract/contract.json`, lists every contract method with its route (`/api/<domain>/<method>`) and its class (`session`, `read`, `evaluate`, `write`). The contract also exports `ApiError` with a `kind`: `locked`, `read_only`, `ledger_unavailable`, `bad_request`, `unknown_method`, `internal`, and `network` for a request that got no answer. A Go backend serves those routes: `POST`, the body is the JSON array of the method's arguments in order, the answer is the result as JSON (`null` for nothing), an error is `{"error":{"kind":"<kind>"}}`, and the session is a cookie the server sets. That backend is read-only: every `write` and `evaluate` method answers `read_only`.

**The client.** Built by iterating the manifest, not as an open-ended proxy, so it has exactly the contract's methods and a call to a method that does not exist cannot become a request. Each method posts its arguments with `credentials: 'same-origin'`, returns the parsed result (`undefined` for a method that returns nothing), and throws `ApiError` with the kind the server sent, or `network` when `fetch` itself fails.

**Chosen at build time.** `vite build` produces the interface for real use, with the HTTP client. `vite build --mode prototype` produces it with the stand-in; the parity scripts build in that mode. `npm --prefix web run dev` keeps the stand-in, PIN `123456`. A new `dev:backend` script runs the dev server with the HTTP client and proxies `/api` to `127.0.0.1:8080`. The stand-in and its dataset are loaded with a dynamic import so they are not in the bundle for real use, and the gate proves it by searching the built files for a sentinel string that exists only in the prototype dataset.

**Why failures need one place.** Nothing in the interface handles a rejected call today. A write is called in seven different patterns (the transaction panel's `write`, `useLineChange`, `actOnSelection`, `useSettingsWrites`, the `announce` helpers of the review and the subscriptions, the closing actions and the budget save, and the PIN form), about sixty call sites, with no shared wrapper; a rejected write becomes an unhandled rejection and a rejected read leaves a blank screen. Rewriting those call sites belongs with the part of the app that will make writes real. Here one function receives every `ApiError`, wired to both `app.config.errorHandler` and the window's `unhandledrejection` event:
- `read_only`: one toast, "Somente leitura por enquanto. Nada foi alterado.", and `useRevisionStore().bump()`, so every screen fetches again and shows the server's state instead of an optimistic one.
- `locked`: the session store becomes locked, which brings the PIN screen back.
- `ledger_unavailable`: a toast, "Dados do banco indisponíveis no momento.", with the action "Tentar de novo".
- anything else: a toast, "Não foi possível carregar os dados.", with the action "Tentar de novo".

"Tentar de novo" bumps the revision counter, which makes the screens fetch again. The toast is the existing one (`useOverlayStore().showToast(message, actions)`); the design has no error variant and none is added. An error that is not an `ApiError` is not swallowed.

**Tests at the right boundary.** The client's own tests stub `fetch`, which is its boundary. Tests of screens keep the repository's rule: the backend is faked with `createFakeApi`, here wrapped by a small test helper that makes every `write` and `evaluate` method of the classification reject with `read_only`, so each write pattern is exercised through a real screen.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The client exposes exactly the methods of the manifest, and each one posts to its route with a JSON array body and `credentials: 'same-origin'`.
- [ ] A 403 answer carrying `read_only` rejects with an `ApiError` of that kind; a rejected `fetch` rejects with kind `network`; a `null` answer to a method that returns nothing resolves to `undefined`.
- [ ] The files produced by `vite build` do not contain the prototype dataset's sentinel string, the files produced by `vite build --mode prototype` do, and `bin/ci` fails if the first ever does.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run parity` still reports every state at or under 0.05%.
- [ ] For each of the seven write patterns, a refused write through a mounted screen shows exactly one toast with the read-only text, bumps the revision counter once, shows no undo toast, and leaves no unhandled rejection.
- [ ] A call rejected with `locked` shows the PIN screen.
- [ ] A read rejected with `ledger_unavailable` shows its toast, and its "Tentar de novo" makes the screen fetch again and render once the read succeeds.
- [ ] A thrown error that is not an `ApiError` still reaches the console and shows no toast.
- [ ] `npm --prefix web run dev` unlocks with `123456` on the stand-in; `dev:backend` sends `/api` to `127.0.0.1:8080`.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` describes the two builds and the two dev scripts.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, parity is unchanged, and the seven refused-write tests pass.

## Tests
- Unit: the client against a stubbed `fetch`: routes, bodies, results, each error kind.
- Unit: the failure function for each kind, and for a non-API error.
- Component: one refused write per write pattern through a mounted screen; a locked answer; a failed read and its retry.
- Build check in the gate: the sentinel string absent from the bundle for real use.
- Parity: the full run, unchanged.
- Each guard is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/api/http/`, `web/src/api/failures.ts`, `web/src/main.ts`, `web/src/stores/session.ts`, `web/src/test/`, `web/vite.config.ts`, `web/package.json`, `web/scripts/parity/`, `bin/ci`, `AGENTS.md`
**Reads only:** `internal/contract/contract.json`, `web/src/api/contract/`, `web/src/api/fake/`, `web/src/stores/overlay.ts`, `web/src/stores/revision.ts`

A new client directory, one new module for failures, the provisioning line in `main.ts`, a lock entry point on the session store, a test helper, the build modes and the gate's bundle check. No screen component and no write call site is edited.
close_reason: web/src/api/http builds the client by iterating the manifest and posts each method to its route with same-origin credentials; the implementation is chosen by a build constant, and the gate proves the build for real use carries neither the stand-in nor the prototype dataset. One function wired to Vue's error handler and to unhandledrejection turns read_only into one toast and a revision bump, locked into the PIN screen, and any other failure into a toast with a retry; no write call site was edited. bin/ci: CI green, 839 tests. Parity: 174 checked, 0 over 0.05%. Each of the seven write patterns has a refused-write test. Known and left: after a refused month close the closing step collapses, which needs an edit to that screen.

title: Compare smaller local models with the outside model for nightly categorisation
description:
## What changes for the user
Every night, the transactions that fixed rules cannot classify are sent to an outside provider's
model: their descriptions, amounts and counterpart names leave the home server, and each call is
billed. The user accepted that for now and asked to know whether a smaller model running at home
could do the same job. Once this lands they have that answer in numbers taken from their own
transactions: which home-run model came closest, how far it trails or beats the outside one, and
whether switching would mean correcting more transactions by hand.

## Outcome
A committed report compares at least three models that run on the user's own hardware against the
outside model on the same set of transactions the user has already confirmed or corrected, and
ends with one recommendation: switch, keep the outside model, or send only the uncertain rows
outside.

## Context
The app assigns each transaction to a budget line, which is one row of the user's monthly budget
(groceries, transport and so on). Fixed rules do most of it: a company that always lands on the
same line is mapped once. What the rules cannot place goes to a language model in a nightly job
that runs with nobody present. The model's answer is applied by itself only when its confidence
is at or above a threshold the user sets, called the auto-apply threshold here; below it the
transaction waits in a queue for the user to decide.

It was decided that the backend reaches the model by calling an HTTP API directly, in the chat
format that outside providers and local model runtimes both accept, so that changing model is a
matter of two configuration values, the base URL and the model name. This bead is the test of
that claim as much as of the models: if a local model needs a different request, the claim is
false and the report must say so.

The user's words when asking for this: outside providers are fine "por enquanto", with a bead to
"avaliar/testar modelos locais menores". Privacy is one reason and cost the other. One guard
already holds on every path: a personal tax number (CPF) is never part of a request, because it
does not help classification.

Two constraints shape the work and are easy to break by accident:

- **The repository is public and the evaluation set is real financial data.** The labelled set
  and every per-row output stay outside the repository, in a directory git ignores. The report
  publishes aggregates only: no description, no counterpart name, no amount per row. Test
  fixtures are synthetic.
- **Which models to try is decided when the work runs, not here.** The set of small models that
  are worth trying changes from month to month, so naming them now would date the bead. The
  criteria fix how many and how they are compared instead.

The evaluation tool may be a script outside the backend, in Python, since it is run by hand a few
times and never deployed. The user was told this and did not object. It must send the same
request the nightly job sends, which is why this bead cannot start before that job exists.

It cannot start yet for a second reason: there is nothing to evaluate against until the user has
used the app long enough to confirm or correct a few hundred categorisations. Both waits are on
work that has no bead at the time of writing, so the bead is parked as blocked with a comment, to
be replaced by dependency edges when the categorisation work is written up.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The evaluation set holds at least 300 transactions whose budget line the user confirmed or
      corrected, spanning at least 3 calendar months, with every CPF removed. The report states
      its size and month span.
- [ ] At least 3 models running on the user's own hardware are measured, at no fewer than 2
      different sizes, beside the outside model in use on that day as the baseline. The report
      names each one with the exact version or tag that was run.
- [ ] Every arm receives the request the nightly job builds, byte for byte except the base URL
      and the model name. The report states this, or lists each difference a model required.
- [ ] For each arm the report gives four figures over the whole set: the share of rows whose
      budget line matches the user's; the share of rows answered at or above the auto-apply
      threshold in force (coverage); the share of matches among those rows; and the share of
      answers that were not valid against the response schema.
- [ ] For each local arm the report records the host's CPU, memory and GPU, and the peak memory
      the model used.
- [ ] Seconds per nightly batch, median of three runs per arm with the arms interleaved, are
      measured **by the review** rather than by whoever implements this, and recorded in the
      report.
- [ ] No file under version control contains a transaction description, a counterpart name or a
      per-row amount from the evaluation set: `git grep` for three descriptions sampled from the
      set returns nothing.
- [ ] The report ends with exactly one recommendation (switch, keep, or route by confidence) and
      the two figures it rests on.
- [ ] Done when: the report is committed at `docs/evaluations/local-models.md` and a reader can
      tell from it alone, without rerunning anything, which local model did best and by how many
      percentage points it trails or beats the baseline at the threshold in force.

## Tests
- Unit: the scoring functions (match share, coverage, match share above the threshold, invalid
  answer share) over a synthetic labelled fixture with known expected values, including a row
  with an invalid answer and a row exactly at the threshold.
- Unit: the loader refuses a set that still carries a CPF-shaped value.
- Manual check: the three measured runs per arm, standing in for an end-to-end test that cannot
  run in CI because the models and the labelled set exist only on the user's machines.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `tools/model-eval/`, `docs/evaluations/local-models.md`
**Reads only:** the backend code that builds the nightly categorisation request

A new, self-contained tool directory (the script, its scoring module and their tests) and one
report. Nothing in the backend or the interface changes; the request builder is read so the tool
sends the same request, and is not edited. If the comparison argues for switching, the switch
itself is a configuration change and belongs to a separate bead.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text: Blocked on work that has no bead yet: the nightly categorisation job whose request this evaluation must reuse, and a few hundred categorisations confirmed or corrected by the user. When that work is written up as beads, replace this status with dependency edges (br dep add finwise-g82 <bead>) and set the status back to open.

title: Give the ledger reader a view that runs every query on one handle and one read-only transaction
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing the person sees changes with this piece, and no answer of the app changes. The app builds a
screen by asking the bank's records several questions, one after another, and a separate collector
replaces those records every night; a screen opened at the moment of the replacement can today be put
together half from yesterday's records and half from today's. This piece gives the part of the app that
reads those records a way to answer many questions from one state of them. The piece after it uses that
for every screen. It also carries every question the app asks today, so if it were wrong the person
would see it at once: a screen that fails to open, or a figure that is no longer what it was.

## Outcome
`internal/ledger` has a view of the snapshot: one handle and one read-only transaction that every one
of the 13 query methods can run on, so that all the queries made through one view see the same snapshot
even when the collector swaps the file meanwhile. The reader's own 13 methods are kept, each as a
