**Decisions already taken, with what lost.**

- Budget lines have a stable id. The wire keeps names, and the budget document gains an optional `id`
  per line; each budget version owns the names its month shows. Why: joining by name means that
  renaming a line silently drops its history from every total. Rejected: names as identity; inferring
  a rename from a line's position; one global name per line.
- The id is a decimal string on the wire, like the other ids the app mints from an integer (a change's
  id, a history step's id, a subscription's id), which keeps recorded answers stable. In TypeScript:
  `id?: string`.
- A transaction's line must exist in the budget in force for the transaction's own month. A line named
  by something that has no month (an establishment's default line, a pot's link, a subscription's
  line) is resolved in the current month. Every line menu says which month it is for. Why: the person
  decided that a transaction of a closed month can still be recategorised, split, excluded and linked,
  since closing freezes the month's budget and not its transactions; a line the month's budget lacks
  would count in no group of that month. Rejected: validating everything against the current month.
- These are two of the places where the server to come departs from the stand-in on purpose: line ids
  instead of names, and a menu and a validation that follow a month. The stand-in is not taught either
  rule. The tests of this work that pin its share are the draft's id tests and the per-caller month
  tests listed below.

**What the id is for, so the draft's obligations make sense.** The server-side rules arrive with the
work that stores budgets in `finwise.db` and answers the budget document, its saves, its scenarios and
the real line menu from there ({{B2}}); none of them is implemented here.

- The id is minted by the server, from an integer that is never reused, when a budget is saved or
  applied. A line without an id is new. Saving a scenario mints nothing.
- A line whose id is kept and whose name changed is a rename: the versions written by that save carry
  the new name, and earlier versions and closed months keep the one they had.
- A save is refused when an id, where present, does not exist or appears twice in the document, as it
  is for an empty or duplicate name or an unknown group.
- The budget document of a month will answer every line with its id. The built-in fees line is in no
  group and no document, so it never appears in a draft; in the line menu it stays an option with a
  name and a group, and menu options carry no id: the wire keeps names.
- Hence the draft: an id must stay on its own line through a copy, a rename, a move up or down and a
  change of amount; a line the person adds has none (the property is absent, not null and not empty);
  removing a line must never leave its id on, or hand it to, another line. A draft that lost an id
  would make the server see a removal and a new line, and removing a line clears it from the
  transactions of the months that lose it (the budget screen's own confirmation says so: "As
  transações dela ficam sem categoria a partir de ..."), which is right when the person removed the
  line and wrong when they only renamed it. A draft that moved an id would give one line another's
  history. Either would be silent.
- What a failed save does to the draft (it keeps it, except a refusal for a closed month, which ends
  the edit) is delivered with the work that teaches the interface the reason of a refusal ({{F6}}), not
  here.

**Which month each menu is for.** `filterOptions` takes one required month, `YYYY-MM`. What the server
will do with it, once it stores budgets, is the reason each caller must send the right one. When the
month's budget has at least one line the menu is that budget's lines, in the stand-in's order
(variable, fixed, reserves, provisions, the fees line, income); when it has none the menu is empty,
with no fees line either. A write on a transaction resolves the line's name in the budget of the
transaction's own month. A write that sets an establishment's default line, a pot's link or a
subscription's line resolves it in the current month. A name the budget of that month does not have is
refused. A transaction shows the name its line has in the budget of its own month. So a menu that
asked for the wrong month offers names the write will refuse, or hides ones it would take.

- The transaction list asks for the month it shows: the month of the query it sends to
  `transactions.list`. That is one month, also when the period filter widens what is listed to three
  months or to the year.
- The list's filter by line also offers every line name its rows carry, because a period of several
  months can hold lines that the month's budget renamed or no longer has, and each row shows the name
  of its own month. "Its rows" are the rows fetched for the month and period, before any filter;
  otherwise choosing one line would take the others out of the menu. A name the menu already has is
  not repeated. Where the added names go in the list and whether they show a group are yours to
  choose; the menu's own lines keep their order.
- The transaction panel asks for the month of the transaction it shows, again whenever that changes,
  and for the current month for the establishment's default line. A default line belongs to the
  establishment, not to the transaction, and is resolved in the current month, so that one menu is for
  the current month while the transaction's line, a split part's line and the refund's line are for
  the transaction's month. When the two months are the same one answer serves all four. While no
  transaction is open the panel has no month and asks nothing. A slower answer for a month it no
  longer shows must not land, the rule `useTransactionList.ts` and `useTransactionDetail.ts` already
  follow for their own reads.
- Each item of the weekly queue asks for its own transaction's month. Answers may be kept per month
  between two revisions, and the tab asks for no month that none of its items has.
- The subscription editor, the settings and the pot links ask for the current month.
- The known tags do not depend on the month; a caller keeps taking them from an answer it holds.
- A menu must not open empty because its answer has not arrived yet. Today the panel has its answer
  long before a transaction is opened, and the queue draws only after its lines arrived. The parity
  check (`npm --prefix web run parity`, which builds the app on the stand-in and measures every screen
  against the design's reference screenshots in a real browser; it is not part of `bin/ci`) opens the
  list's menus and the queue's as soon as the screen is up, in its states `inicio-menu-linha`,
  `inicio-linha-alterada` and `revisao-linha-escolhida`, and in the last two picks a line.

**Every menu asks again when the revision is bumped.** Every screen that shows what the person
authored fetches again on a bump. The list, the weekly tab and the settings (which ask at each
opening) already do. Two do not, and this work fixes them, because they would otherwise show a stale
menu after the very writes they offer: the transaction panel, whose line menus and tag menu come from
an answer loaded once when the frame was mounted, and the subscription screen, whose line menu comes
from an answer loaded once at setup. After this work both ask again on every bump, for the months
they hold. The other places that do not refetch on a bump (the net worth screen, the pots list and a
pot's page) are fixed by the work that stores a pot's bucket and its linked lines ({{S2}}) and are not
touched here.

**The stand-in follows the new types and nothing else.** It keeps an `id` it is given on a line
through a save, an applied scenario and a saved scenario, and answers it back in the document and in
the scenarios; it mints none, so a line saved without an id is stored without one, and the prototype's
dataset has none. It accepts the month of the line menu and keeps answering the menu of its current
month's budget whatever month is asked: making the menu follow the month is the server's rule, and the
stand-in validates almost nothing. Unused parameters are a type error in this project
(`noUnusedParameters`), so the stand-in's method either leaves the parameter out or names it with a
leading underscore. Its answers over an empty ledger must stay equal to the server's, which a test
already checks.

**What the Go side needs so the gate stays green.** Once the manifest says the menu takes one
argument, the router answers `bad_request` to the empty array every Go test sends today. This is part
of this work, not a follow-up.

- `readTransactionFilterOptions` reads its month with `onlyMonthArgument`, before it touches the
  ledger, and answers exactly what it answers today. The lines stay empty until the server stores
  budgets and answers the menu from them ({{B2}}).
- `readCases` in `internal/api/conformance_test.go`, the list every registered read must have a case
  in, has `{"transactions.filterOptions", "[]"}` (the arguments in backquotes). It becomes
  `["2026-03"]`, the month of the clock the invented ledgers run on (`fixtureNow`, 2026-03-20). Keep
  the entry's written shape: a test of the interface finds these cases by it.
- A golden file is named after its arguments (`goldenName` in `internal/api/golden_test.go`): the two
  files `transactions.filterOptions.json`, under `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/` and `empty/`,
  become `transactions.filterOptions.2026-03.json` with the same bytes, and the old names are deleted,
  or `TestEveryGoldenFileHasACase` fails. This rename is the only change to the files of `empty/`, and
  in `full/` nothing else changes here either. `go test ./internal/api -run
  TestEveryAnswerMatchesItsGoldenFile -update` writes the new ones; it refuses to run while
  `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set.
- `internal/api/transactions_test.go` calls the method with `[]` in two tests, and
  `internal/api/realsnapshot_test.go` in one.
- Two tests of the interface read the Go side and must keep passing. `web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`
  parses `readCases` out of the Go test sources, calls the stand-in with the same arguments and
  requires its answer to equal the file under `empty/`. `web/src/test/replay-sweep.test.ts` mounts the
  whole app over the golden files (`replayApi` in `web/src/test/replay.ts`) and fails on any call with
  no recorded answer. Over both recorded ledgers the month the list shows, the month of every listed
  transaction and the current month are all `2026-03`, so the one case covers every call the sweep
  makes; if a caller asked for any other month there, the sweep would say so.

**Privacy.** `internal/api/realsnapshot_test.go` is the one test that opens a real ledger, and it runs
only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file. A real ledger is a person's whole financial history
and this repository is public. A real snapshot may be opened read-only; no value from it (an amount, a
description, a name, a document, an id) is ever printed, logged, or copied into a file, a commit, a
bead or a pull request; a count may be shown to the person running the test and goes into no file.
That test's own header counts a month of the ledger among those values. This work only gives its call
the month argument it now needs: any valid month does, since the handler does not use it yet, and the
argument is neither printed nor put in a failure message. Nothing here needs a real ledger to be
proved. Fixtures are invented.

**Out of scope.** Storing a budget, minting an id, validating a save, the real line menu and the fees
line on the server; validating a line against a month in any write; `BudgetLineOption`, which gains no
id; the stand-in's rules; a menu of lines per row of the list; the budget screen's look.

**Conventions.** Work in your own git worktree on a branch of your own and stop at local commits:
atomic, Conventional Commits, no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a
commit message. The manifest is regenerated with `npm --prefix web run contract` and committed with
the type change that caused it. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese; everything else in the
repository is English. A design value in a component comes from a token; this work changes no style.
Money is integer cents and no float may appear in the money path (`internal/api` has a test that fails
on one), and every SQL statement over the app's database is a registered constant; this work adds
neither money arithmetic nor SQL. The backend is faked at the API boundary with `createFakeApi`; a
test that needs to see which month a menu asked for wraps that one method of it, as
`web/src/api/refused-writes.test.ts` wraps `budget.view`.

mints and that a new line has none; `TransactionsApi.filterOptions` requires one `YearMonth`.

Wide and shallow: about fourteen source files, each changed by a few lines, across the contract, the
stand-in, five callers and the list's filter in the interface, and one Go handler, with their tests,
the generated manifest and two renamed golden files. It is one bead because it cannot be narrowed
without leaving the gate red: a required argument changes the type every caller compiles against, the
argument count the router enforces and the name of the recorded answers at once. The label is
`critical` for the id alone: a draft that drops or moves one fails silently, and only once budgets are
stored. `web/src/screens/budget/useBudgetDraft.ts` is listed because a test may find a hole in it; as
read today it already carries a field through every edit. The budget screens, the line menu's own
component, the router and the reader are read, not changed.

title: Editing the budget against a read-only backend asks the same refused question forever
description:
## What changes for the user
Against the real backend, which only reads for now, pressing "Editar budget" makes the app ask the server the same refused question about twenty-five times a second, without end, with the read-only message stuck on screen. Opening "Cenários" shows the read-only message before the person has done anything, and the screen stays blank where the scenario's impact should be. After this lands, pressing "Editar budget" shows the read-only message once and leaves the budget as it was, and opening "Cenários" does the same and returns to the budget.

## Outcome
A refused evaluation of a budget draft or of a scenario ends the editing surface that asked for it, with one read-only toast and no further request.

## Context
finwise's interface runs against a backend that is read-only for now. Every write and every evaluation of the contract answers a `read_only` error, and one function (`web/src/api/failures.ts`) turns that into a toast ("Somente leitura por enquanto. Nada foi alterado.") and a bump of the revision counter, so that every screen fetches again and none keeps showing a state the server refused. No call site catches errors itself, on purpose.

Two screens ask for an evaluation, which is refused like a write because the budget's arithmetic is not built on the server yet:

- `web/src/screens/budget/BudgetScreen.vue` watches the selected month, the revision counter and the budget draft together, and calls `api.budget.view(month, draft)` whenever one of them changes. In edit mode the draft is set, so the call is refused; the refusal bumps the revision counter; the watcher fires again with the same draft; and so on, forever. Measured in Chromium against the built backend over a real ledger: 127 refused calls in five seconds, still going.
- `web/src/screens/budget/ScenariosScreen.vue` calls `api.budget.evaluateScenario` as soon as it opens. That is refused once, the toast shows although the person only opened a screen, and the impact never arrives.

The decision taken for both, to be confirmed by the user: an editing surface that cannot evaluate ends itself. The budget leaves edit mode, discarding the draft it was just handed, and shows its read view again. The scenarios screen returns to the budget. Each shows the read-only toast exactly once. This follows the choice made for the read-only backend as a whole, that a refused change is one toast and the screen as it was, and adds no "unavailable" state of its own.

The fix belongs in the two screens: each recognises the `read_only` refusal of its own evaluation, ends itself, and lets the error go on to the central function, which shows the toast. The central function is not changed, and an error that is not `read_only` is not caught.

Tests already exist for refusals through mounted screens (`web/src/api/refused-writes.test.ts`, with `web/src/test/readOnly.ts` wrapping the stand-in so that every write and evaluation is refused as the backend refuses it). The sweep over the backend's recorded answers (`web/src/test/replay-sweep.test.ts`) tolerates a `read_only` refusal on the scenarios route because of this defect; once the scenarios screen no longer stays on a refused evaluation, that tolerance is removed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Mount the Budget screen on the stand-in wrapped by the read-only helper and press "Editar budget".
2. Observed: `budget.view` is called with the draft again and again, each call refused, and the toast is shown each time.
3. Expected: one refused call, one toast, the screen out of edit mode, and no further call with a draft.
4. Mount the scenarios screen on the same stand-in.
5. Observed: one refused `budget.evaluateScenario`, a toast, and no impact on screen.
6. Expected: one refused call, one toast, and the route back at the budget.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After "Editar budget" over the read-only stand-in, `budget.view` is called with a draft exactly once, the read-only toast is shown exactly once, the screen is out of edit mode, and no call with a draft follows within the next ten bumps of the revision counter.
- [ ] After opening the scenarios screen over the read-only stand-in, `budget.evaluateScenario` is called exactly once, the read-only toast is shown exactly once, and the current route is the budget.
- [ ] Over the plain stand-in, editing the budget and opening the scenarios screen behave as before, and `npm --prefix web run parity` still reports every state at or under 0.05%.
- [ ] An evaluation that fails with an error other than `read_only` does not end edit mode and still reaches the central function.
- [ ] The sweep over the backend's recorded answers no longer tolerates a refusal on any route.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, parity is unchanged, and both regression tests fail when their fix is removed.

## Tests
- Component, regression: a refused evaluation through the mounted Budget screen ends edit mode with one call and one toast.
- Component, regression: a refused evaluation through the mounted scenarios screen returns to the budget with one call and one toast.
- Component: another kind of failure does not end edit mode.
- Component: the sweep over the recorded answers, with its tolerance removed.
- Parity: the full run, unchanged.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/screens/budget/BudgetScreen.vue`, `web/src/screens/budget/ScenariosScreen.vue`, `web/src/api/refused-writes.test.ts`, `web/src/test/replay-sweep.test.ts`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/failures.ts`, `web/src/test/readOnly.ts`, `web/src/stores/`, `bin/ci`

Two screens each learn to end themselves on a refused evaluation, with a regression test each, and one tolerance leaves the sweep.
close_reason: BudgetScreen.vue discards the draft when the evaluation of a draft is refused, and ScenariosScreen.vue returns to the budget when its evaluation is refused; both rethrow, so the central function still shows the one toast and no other kind of error is caught. Regression tests through the mounted screens over the read-only stand-in: before the fix the budget made 71 calls with a draft where one was expected and the scenarios screen stayed on its route; both fail again with their fix removed. The replay sweep no longer tolerates a refused call on any route; it answers the one scenario evaluation from the stand-in so that screen is swept drawn. bin/ci: CI green, 934 tests. Parity: 174 checked, 0 over 0.05%; no template changed.

title: Turn a ledger row into the transaction the app lists
description:
## What changes for the user
The bank's records are not the list a person expects to read. A card purchase and a bank debit carry opposite signs, a purchase abroad shows its price in another currency, the tax on it arrives as a separate row, paying the card bill looks like spending twice, and moving money into a savings pot looks like an expense. After this lands the app can turn those records into one line per purchase in reais, with the tax under its purchase, with transfers between the person's own accounts set apart, and with pot movements out of the general list. No record is ever dropped without being accounted for.

## Outcome
A Go package of pure functions, `internal/txrules`, that takes the rows the ledger reader returns for a period and gives back the transactions the app lists, each with its kind, signed amount in cents, Brazil day, counterpart and establishment key, plus a tally that places every input row in exactly one destination.

## Context
finwise is a personal finance app over a SQLite ledger collected from the person's banks. A Go package, `internal/ledger`, already reads that ledger and returns rows faithfully, with amounts in integer cents and the raw provider fields parsed; it interprets nothing. This bead is the interpretation. It does no SQL and no I/O.

**The app's convention.** An amount is signed and negative means money out, on every kind of account. A day is `YYYY-MM-DD` in America/Sao_Paulo. The interface's contract for a transaction is `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`; its kinds and subtypes are the vocabulary this package maps to.

**Direction and sign.** The row's `type` (`DEBIT` or `CREDIT`) is only a direction, and the sign of the stored amount is inverted between account types: on a `BANK` account a debit is stored negative; on a `CREDIT` account (a card) a purchase is a positive debit and a payment or refund a negative credit. Direction comes from `type` together with the account type, never from the stored sign alone.

**Foreign purchases.** The stored amount is in the original currency. The value in reais is `raw.amountInAccountCurrency` when present. The app amount is the value in reais; the original amount and currency are kept for display.

**Day.** `date` is a UTC timestamp on every row; convert before taking the day. `creditCardMetadata.purchaseDate` exists on few rows, so `date` is the date.

**Kind.** Decided with the user: bank rows are split by payment method (PIX, boleto, and "Outros" for the rest: TED, TEF, debit, fees); card rows are those of `CREDIT` accounts. The kind is read from the account type, `raw.operationType` and `raw.paymentData.paymentMethod` together, because `operationType` alone lies: a bank row may be typed `OUTROS` and carry `paymentMethod` `PIX`. Vocabulary seen on bank accounts: `PIX`, `BOLETO`, `TED`, `TEF`, `CARTAO`, `FOLHA_PAGAMENTO`, `CONVENIO_ARRECADACAO`, `PACOTE_TARIFA_SERVICOS`, `ENCARGOS_JUROS_CHEQUE_ESPECIAL`, `TRANSFERENCIA_SALDO_RESERVADO`, `RESGATE_APLIC_FINANCEIRA`, `RENDIMENTO_APLIC_FINANCEIRA`, `OUTROS`; `paymentMethod` is one of `PIX`, `BOLETO`, `TED`, `TEF`, `OTHER` and exists only on bank rows. On card accounts: `PAGAMENTO`, `ESTORNO`, `TARIFA`, `PAGAMENTO_FATURA`, `OUTROS`, or none.

**Card rows typed `OUTROS`.** `operationType` cannot be the rule across banks: on C6 `OUTROS` is almost only tax, on Itaú it is everything the bank does not classify. Hiding only `PAGAMENTO_FATURA` would leave Itaú's bill payments counted as spending, and hiding `OUTROS` would drop real purchases. The groups, each row in exactly one:
- A tax row named after its purchase (C6): its amount is exactly 3.5% of a purchase with the same name on the same card within 3 days. It is attached to that purchase and leaves the list.
- An explicit tax row (Itaú): the description is `IOF INTERNACIONAL`. It is attached to the foreign purchase of the same day on the same card. The sources give no rule for a day with several foreign purchases: attach only when exactly one candidate exists, otherwise keep the row listed.
- A purchase abroad typed `OUTROS` (Itaú): an ordinary purchase.
- A bill payment seen from the card (Itaú): the description is `PAGAMENTO COM SALDO`. It is a movement.
- An early-payment discount: the description is `Desc Antecipa Parcelas`. The user confirmed it is a discount for paying instalments ahead; it is a credit under fees and interest.
- A credit with no keyword on the C6 card: the user confirmed these are refunds.
- A partial cancellation (Itaú): a refund. The sources give no keyword for it.

**Movements.** Listed, under their own kind, and never counted as an expense or as income by a caller: a bill payment (from the card side `PAGAMENTO_FATURA` or `PAGAMENTO COM SALDO`; the bank-account side has no written rule), and a transfer between the person's own accounts, recognised when the counterpart's document is one of the person's own in the ledger's `identities`. Savings-pot movements (`TRANSFERENCIA_SALDO_RESERVADO`, and Mercado Pago's `RESGATE_APLIC_FINANCEIRA` rows whose description starts with `Rendimentos`) leave the general list and are returned separately, per account, for the pot they belong to.

**Counterpart and establishment.** The ledger has no merchant on any row. A PIX or a boleto carries `paymentData.payer` and `.receiver`, each with a name and a document: the counterpart is the other party, its key is the document, and it is a person when the document has 11 digits and a company when it has 14. A card purchase has only its description: the display name comes from it and the key is the normalised text. Two descriptions that differ only in letter case, spacing or a trailing instalment marker such as `03/10` share a key. A document is another person's personal data: it is a key, it is never logged.

**What the sources leave open.** For each of these, write the smallest rule that is safe, state it in a comment, and report how many rows it matched on a real ledger, as a count only: the bank-account side of a bill payment; the keyword of a partial cancellation; the explicit tax row on a day with several foreign purchases; how far text normalisation goes. The safe default everywhere: a row no rule recognises stays in the list as an ordinary transaction of kind "Outros". Dropping it is the failure that matters.

**The tally.** Processing a period returns, beside the list, how many input rows were listed, attached to a purchase as tax, or returned as pot movements. Every input row id is in exactly one of the three.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `BANK` debit of 50.00 yields -5000 and a `BANK` credit +5000; a `CREDIT`-account debit of 50.00 yields -5000 and a `CREDIT`-account credit +5000; each holds whichever sign the fixture stored.
- [ ] A purchase of 10.00 in USD with 55.00 in the account currency yields -5500 and keeps `1000` and `USD` as the original.
- [ ] A row dated `2026-03-01T02:30:00Z` has the day `2026-02-28`.
- [ ] A bank row typed `OUTROS` with `paymentMethod` `PIX` is a PIX.
- [ ] A row of 7.00 named like a purchase of 200.00 on the same card two days later is attached to it and absent from the list; the same row at 7.01, or four days later, or on another card, stays listed.
- [ ] `IOF INTERNACIONAL` on a day with exactly one foreign purchase on that card is attached; with two it stays listed.
- [ ] `PAGAMENTO_FATURA` and `PAGAMENTO COM SALDO` rows are movements; `Desc Antecipa Parcelas` is a positive fee credit; a keyword-less credit on a C6 card is a refund.
- [ ] A PIX out whose receiver's document is in `identities` is a movement between own accounts; the same PIX to another document is a PIX to a counterpart.
- [ ] `TRANSFERENCIA_SALDO_RESERVADO` rows and `RESGATE_APLIC_FINANCEIRA` rows starting with `Rendimentos` are absent from the list and present in the pot movements of their account.
- [ ] A PIX out names its receiver, is keyed by the receiver's document, and is a person for an 11-digit document and a company for a 14-digit one.
- [ ] `ACME STORE 03/10`, `acme  store` and `ACME STORE` share one establishment key.
- [ ] A row with an `operationType` no rule knows is listed as "Outros".
- [ ] For every fixture and for randomly generated inputs, each input row id is in exactly one of: listed, attached as tax, pot movement.
- [ ] The package imports neither `database/sql` nor `os`.
- [ ] A test skipped unless `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` is set runs every month of a real snapshot through the rules and logs only counts: the tally, the rows per kind, and the rows matched by each rule left open above.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.` and the opt-in run reports a tally whose three parts sum to the number of input rows for every month.

## Tests
- Unit: one table-driven test per rule, each with rows that must match and rows that must not.
- Property: the tally invariant over generated inputs.
- Integration, opt-in: every month of a real snapshot, counts only.
- Each rule is broken once on purpose and the failing test named in the report.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/txrules/`
**Reads only:** `internal/ledger/`, `internal/money/`, `internal/brday/`, `web/src/api/contract/transactions.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/rules.ts`, `bin/ci`

One new package of pure functions and its tests. If a rule needs a raw field the reader does not parse yet, that field is added to the reader's row type with its test and nothing else in `internal/ledger` changes.
close_reason: internal/txrules turns the reader's rows into the transactions the app lists: direction from type and account type, foreign purchases in reais with the original kept, the Brazil day, kinds read from operationType and paymentMethod together, card rows sorted by their own text and direction, movements, pot movements set apart, counterpart and establishment key, and a tally that places every input row in exactly one destination. bin/ci: CI green. The tally invariant holds over fixtures and over random inputs, and the opt-in run over a real snapshot balanced every month. Rules written where the sources were silent, each stated in a comment beside the code: the bank side of a bill payment by its text; a card credit with no operation type that names a payment is a bill payment; refund stems for a cancellation; an explicit tax row attaches only when exactly one foreign purchase exists on that card that day; text normalisation stops at case, accents, spacing and a trailing instalment marker. A tax row is paired only within the rows given, so a caller reads the days around its period.

title: Keep subscriptions made from card purchases and derive each one's cycle, cost, next charge and marks from the card's charges
description:
## What changes for the user
Against real data the Assinaturas screen is empty today: the list has nothing in it, "Nova assinatura"
offers no purchase to pick, and anything the person tries to change is answered with "read only". After
this lands the person opens "Nova assinatura", picks one of this month's card purchases, and it becomes a
subscription the app keeps. From the card's own charges the app works out how often it is charged, what
that costs per month and per year, when the next charge is due and what the last charges were, and it
marks a price that rose, a yearly plan about to renew, and a subscription that charged again after being
marked to cancel. The person sets its status, its budget line, the day to review it and a note, and takes
any of that back with "Desfazer". A subscription that has no budget line shows a dash where the line
would be. If this were wrong the person would not get an error: they would read a monthly total that does
not match their card, or a plan called monthly that is charged once a year.

## Outcome
The app's database has a `subscriptions` table, created by the migration `0006_subscriptions`. A new
package of pure rules, `internal/subrules`, turns the charges of one subscription into its cycle, its
amount and previous amount, its next charge, its monthly and yearly equivalents, its marks and its charge
history, in integer cents. `subscriptions.list`, `subscriptions.detail` and `subscriptions.candidates`
answer from the ledger and the app's database; `subscriptions.recurring` keeps answering an empty list.
Seven writes have handlers: `create`, `setStatus`, `setLine`, `setReviewDate` and `setNote` record a change
that can be undone, and `acceptSuggestion` and `rejectSuggestion` answer null. In the contract a
subscription's `line` is nullable, the manifest says so, and the three places of the interface that render
it show a subscription that has none.

## Context
**The app and its words.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person. *The ledger* is a SQLite
*snapshot* that a separate collector fills from the banks every night; the app opens it read-only and
never writes to it. *The app's database* is `finwise.db`, a second SQLite file the server opens when it is
started with `--db`; everything the person types lives there. *The contract* is the TypeScript description
of the 82 methods the interface calls (`web/src/api/contract/`); *the manifest*,
`internal/contract/contract.json`, is that contract generated for Go (route, class, argument and result
schemas of each method) by `npm --prefix web run contract`, versioned and never edited by hand. *The
stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/` that the design prototype runs on; it is
the only existing statement of how writes behave, and where this bead does not say otherwise its behaviour
is the rule. *The journal* is the record of every change made to the app's database, with its author,
from which a change is undone. *The index* is the small table in which the app's database remembers the
transactions it has seen, each under a key of its own.

**What exists today (checked in the code).**
- `internal/api/subscriptions.go` registers four reads in `registerSubscriptions`, which is one of the
  entries of `domainRegistrations` in `internal/api/reads.go`. `subscriptions.list` answers zero totals, no
  group and `suggestion: null`; `subscriptions.detail` answers null for any id; `subscriptions.candidates`
  and `subscriptions.recurring` answer `[]` through `readNothingListed`. The file's own comment says that
  spotting repeating purchases "is not decided and belongs with that side".
- `internal/api/subscriptions_test.go` adds five entries to `readCases` and holds four tests. Two of them
  assert what this bead reverses: `TestSubscriptionsAnswerAsAFreshInstallOverBothLedgers` expects
  `candidates` to be `[]` over the full invented ledger, and
  `TestARepeatingLookingPurchaseIsNotOfferedAsACandidate` expects a card purchase not to be offered.
- The seven writes (`subscriptions.create`, `acceptSuggestion`, `rejectSuggestion`, `setStatus`,
  `setLine`, `setReviewDate`, `setNote`, all of class `write` in
  `web/src/api/contract/classification.ts`) are refused with `read_only`.
- `internal/txrules` interprets the ledger's rows into the list the app shows. A listed
  `txrules.Transaction` carries `Kind` (`KindCard` is `"cartao"`), a signed `Amount` in cents (negative is
  money out) that already includes any tax row folded into the purchase, `Tax`, `Original` (a foreign
  amount, kept for display), `Unconverted`, `Movement`, `Refund`, `Fee`, `Posted`, `Day` and
  `EstablishmentKey`. A tax row attached to a purchase leaves the list. `internal/api/card.go`
  (`loadCard`) already reads and interprets the whole ledger in one pass with
  `reader.CleanTransactions(ctx, wholeLedger)` and `interpretRows`; `interpretPeriod` in
  `internal/api/transactions_period.go` interprets a period widened by the three days in which a tax row
  is paired with its purchase.
- `internal/brday` names a day and a month in Brazil time and has no arithmetic on days or months.
  `internal/cardrules/calendar.go` keeps its own, in UTC, with a comment that says why.
- `internal/api/messages.go` opens with "Everything a person reads that the server writes lives in this
  file, in Brazilian Portuguese."
- The interface renders a subscription's line in three places, all under `web/src/screens/assinaturas/`
  (there is no `web/src/components/subscriptions/`): the "Linha do budget" cell of `SubscriptionRow.vue`
  (`{{ row.line }}`, shown from 1200px), `rowSubtitle` in `subscriptionText.ts` (the line under the name
  below 1200px, `` `${row.cycle} · ${brl(row.monthlyEquivalent)} por mês · ${row.line}` ``) and the button of
  `SubscriptionEditor.vue` (`{{ subscription.line }} ▾`), which also passes the line to `openLineMenu` as
  the current item. `openLineMenu` in `web/src/components/transactions/useLineChange.ts` already takes
  `current: string | null`.
- In the stand-in, `FakeSubscription` (`web/src/api/fake/model.ts`) stores the cycle, the amount, the next
  charge, a previous amount and two flags as seeded data; `subscription-rules.ts` computes the equivalents,
  the totals, the groups and the marks from them, and invents the charge history by stepping back from
  the stored next charge. `subscriptionFrom` gives a new subscription the purchase's line or the literal
  `'Assinaturas'`.

**What this builds on, delivered by earlier work.** None of it is in the repository when this is written;
read it as it landed.
- The migrations runner and the statement registry of `internal/authored`, the only package that executes
  SQL against the app's database ({{F1}}): SQL files embedded from `internal/authored/migrations/` are
  recorded by name and checksum in `schema_migrations` and every missing one is applied at start, in name
  order, each in one transaction; every SQL statement is a registered constant that a test prepares
  against the migrated schema, and a test fails on one that is not registered.
- The recorder ({{F2}}), the layer through which every change to a journaled table is written: a closed,
  hand-written registry names each journaled table and its shape, every effect lands in the journal, a
  test fails when a statement changes a journaled table outside it, and undo restores a change's effects
  by inverse, refusing when a later change that is still in force touched the same thing.
- The per-request views ({{F3b}}): a handler receives one view of the ledger (one snapshot for the whole
  request) and one of the app's database (one read-only transaction for a read; without `--db` an empty
  view that answers nothing, so read code has one path), and the clock is required: "today" and "the
  current month" are the Brazil day and month of the instant in the request's context, and a source test
  forbids `time.Now` in the non-test files of `internal/api` and of the rule packages.
- Write dispatch ({{F4c}}): a write that has a handler has its arguments validated against the method's
  schema from the manifest, runs inside one immediate transaction with a recorder that already holds the
  facts of the change (author, method, instant, Brazil day), and is committed by the dispatcher; any
  failure rolls everything back and answers `internal`. A write without a handler, or a server without
  `--db`, answers `read_only` before the body is read. The same work brings the error kind `refused`
  (HTTP 409, `{"error":{"kind":"refused","reason":"..."}}`, the reason from a closed list), the method
  `changes.undo`, and a test that walks the manifest and requires every write to have a handler or to be
  named in an explicit list, `writesWithoutHandler`.
- The write conformance harness ({{F5}}): every write has a case of exactly one mode (a recorded change,
  whose answer validates against the manifest, whose effects match a golden file under
  `internal/api/testdata/golden/writes/` and whose undo returns a canonical dump of every journaled table
  to the dump taken before; or nothing to do, a null answer that adds no row to the journal), one refusal
  case per reason, the package `internal/authored/authoredtest` that builds invented states of the app's
  database, a third state for read conformance (the full invented ledger with an invented authored state,
  cases in `authoredReadCases`, golden files in `internal/api/testdata/golden/full-authored/`), and a
  test that runs every case and proves nothing it holds reaches the logs.
- The budget's tables and lines ({{B2}}): `lines(id, builtin)` gives every budget line a stable integer id,
  a budget is a list of versions each valid from a month on, a line's name belongs to a version, and a
  line's name is resolved to its id (and back) in the budget in force for a given month. The line menu,
  `transactions.filterOptions(month)`, lists that month's lines, and every caller already sends the month
  its menu is for ({{B1}}: the subscription page asks for the current month and reloads on a new
  revision, so `AssinaturaScreen.vue` needs no change here).
- The transactions' tables and the index ({{T1}}): `tx_index` and `tx_ids` give each transaction a key of
  its own (`tx_key`) and map the provider's ids to it; `tx_state` holds what the person or a rule decided
  about a transaction (its line, its exclusion); `establishments` holds a nickname per establishment key;
  and the transaction reads merge all of that into what the list shows. A write names a transaction by
  the provider's id, resolves it through the same interpreted ledger read the list uses, in the request's
  snapshot, and creates or refreshes its index row. An id that read does not list (an unknown id, a tax
  row folded into its purchase, a pot movement) is unknown.

**The table.** One migration file, `internal/authored/migrations/0006_subscriptions.sql`. The name is
fixed; migrations are recorded by name, so it may be applied to a database that already holds a
higher-numbered one. The columns are the starting point, and a column may be added here if a test shows
it is needed:

| column | holds | constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | the subscription's id | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, so an id is never reused; a decimal string on the wire (`"1"`, `"2"`) |
| `establishment_key` | the establishment the subscription is tied to | not null, unique |
| `created_from_tx_key` | the key of the purchase it was made from | not null, foreign key to `tx_index` |
| `created_day` | that purchase's day, as it was at creation | not null |
| `created_cents` | that purchase's amount as a magnitude in cents, tax included, as it was at creation | not null, `CHECK` not negative |
| `name` | the name it was created under | not null |
| `line_id` | its budget line, or null | foreign key to `lines` |
| `status` | one of the contract's four words: `Manter`, `Analisar`, `Backup e cancelar`, `Cancelar` | not null, `CHECK` on the four |
| `status_day` | the Brazil day the status was last set | not null |
| `review_on` | the day to review it | not null |
| `note` | the note | not null, empty by default |

For the recorder it is an attribute table: one row of independent facts per key, the key being `id`. An
effect is one column changing. Creating a row is itself a unit, so a later change to any column of that
row that is still in force makes the change that created it stale. No history step is written for a
subscription; history belongs to transactions.

**Which purchases can become a subscription.** A subscription is made by hand from a card purchase of the
current month. The eligible purchases are the listed transactions of the current month that are on a
card (`Kind` is `KindCard`), are money out (a negative amount), are not a movement (a movement between
own accounts or a bill payment), are not a fee, are not unconverted (a foreign row the ledger gives no
value in reais for), are not excluded (an exclusion counts only once it has a reason; one switched on
with no reason yet still counts), and whose establishment key has no subscription. A row the bank still
reports as pending is listed and is eligible like any other.

`subscriptions.candidates` answers one of them per establishment: the newest (on the same day, the one
with the lower id). The candidates are ordered newest first; two candidates of the same day keep the
order the transaction list gives them, as in the stand-in, which walks the list. At most twelve are
answered. Each is `{transactionId, name, amount}`: the provider's id, the name the transaction list shows
for that transaction (take it from the same function the list uses, so that a nickname shows here as soon
as nicknames exist), and the magnitude of the amount, tax included. The filter comes first and the pick
second: when the newest purchase of an establishment is excluded, the next eligible one is its candidate.
With no app's database nothing is a subscription and nothing is excluded, so the candidates come from the
ledger alone.

**`subscriptions.create(transactionId)`.** It accepts any eligible purchase, whether or not it is among
the twelve shown and whether or not it is the newest of its establishment. For anything else it answers
null and records nothing: an id the ledger does not list, a purchase of another month, a credit, a
movement, a fee, an unconverted or excluded row, a transaction that is not on a card, or a purchase whose
establishment key already has a subscription. Otherwise it gets the purchase's key from the index
(creating or refreshing its index row), inserts the row and answers `{changeId, name}`:

- `name`: the name the candidate list shows for the purchase at that moment. It is stored and does not
  follow a later nickname.
- `created_day`, `created_cents`: the purchase's day and the magnitude of its amount.
- `line_id`: the line stored for the purchase itself, or null when it has none. A suggestion waiting for
  review is not a line. The purchase is of the current month, so its line is one the current month's
  budget has.
- `status`: `Analisar`. `status_day`: today.
- `review_on`: today plus three months, the day number kept and held to the last day of a shorter month
  (2026-11-28 gives 2027-02-28; 2026-11-30 gives 2027-02-28; 2026-03-20 gives 2026-06-20).
- `note`: empty.

Undoing the change removes the row and the purchase is a candidate again. A subscription made again
after that gets a new id. Writes queue on the database's write lock, so of two `create` for one
establishment the second finds the key taken and answers null; the unique constraint is the backstop.

**The derivation, as an algorithm.** `internal/subrules` takes plain values and returns plain values; it
opens nothing, reads no clock and knows neither HTTP nor SQL, as `internal/txrules`, `internal/cardrules`
and `internal/potrules` do. For one subscription `internal/api` hands it: the eligible rows as plain
values (day, magnitude in cents, and the foreign amount with its tax when the row has one), the stored
`created_day` and `created_cents`, the status and its day, and today.

1. *The rows.* From the whole ledger, interpreted in one pass in the request's snapshot (so a tax row is
   already folded into its purchase): the listed transactions with the subscription's establishment key
   that are on a card, are money out, are not a movement, are not unconverted and are not excluded. A
   debit of the same establishment on a bank account is not a charge. The index is never the source of a
   figure: days and amounts come from the ledger.
2. *The charges.* One charge per day: rows of the same day are added together. A charge is a day, an
   amount (the sum of its rows' magnitudes, tax included) and a foreign amount. It carries the foreign
   amount (`originalAmount` as `originalAmountOf` in `internal/api/transactions_wire.go` writes it, and
   `iof`, the folded tax as a positive figure) only when it is made of exactly one row and that row has
   both a foreign amount and a folded tax, which is the stand-in's condition in `subscriptionFrom`; a
   charge made of several rows carries none. Order the charges by day.
3. *No charge left.* When step 2 gives none (the purchase was excluded since, the ledger stopped listing
   it, or the bank reworded the establishment so its key changed), the stored `created_day` and
   `created_cents` stand in for one charge, with no foreign amount.
4. *Amount and previous amount.* The amount is the latest charge's. The previous amount is that of the
   charge before it; with one charge there is none.
5. *Cycle.* With fewer than two charge days: monthly. Otherwise take the gaps in whole days between
   consecutive charge days, keep the last six gaps at most (the most recent ones), sort them, and take
   their median: the middle one for an odd count, the lower of the two middle ones for an even count
   (position `(count - 1) / 2` of the sorted gaps, counting from zero, in integer division). The cycle is
   the one whose length is nearest to that median, the shorter on a tie:

   | length in days | cycle on the wire | months | medians that fall on it |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | 30 | `Mensal` | 1 | 1 to 60 |
   | 91 | `Trimestral` | 3 | 61 to 136 |
   | 182 | `Semestral` | 6 | 137 to 273 |
   | 365 | `Anual` | 12 | 274 to 547 |
   | 730 | `Bienal` | 24 | 548 and above |

   A median is a whole number of days and the midpoints between two lengths are 60.5, 136.5, 273.5 and
   547.5, so with these five lengths no median is equally far from two of them. The rule "the shorter on a
   tie" is still how the comparison is written (the shorter length wins when the distances are equal), so
   the result never depends on the order the lengths are tried in; the boundaries in the last column are
   what a test can pin.
6. *Next charge.* The latest charge's day plus the cycle's months, the day number kept and held to the
   last day of a shorter month. It is computed from the latest charge and nothing else: a subscription
   whose charges stopped answers a next charge that is already past.
7. *Equivalents.* Monthly: the amount divided by the cycle's months, rounded half up to the cent.
   Yearly: the amount times twelve divided by the cycle's months, rounded half up to the cent. Amounts
   here are magnitudes and never negative, so there is no negative half; the halves to pin are positive
   (0.03 on a `Semestral` cycle is 0.01 a month; 10.01 on a `Bienal` cycle is 5.01 a year). No float: the
   stand-in's `Math.round(x * 100) / 100` is restated in integer cents.
8. *Marks*, in this order, each `{text, tone}`:
   - `Preço subiu`, tone `warning`, when there is a previous amount and it is lower than the amount. A
     price that fell or stayed gives no mark.
   - for a cycle of twelve months or more (`Anual`, `Bienal`), when the whole days from today to the next
     charge are from 0 to 30, tone `warning`: `Renova hoje` for 0, `Renova em 1 dia` for 1,
     `Renova em N dias` for 2 to 30 (`Renova em 9 dias`, `Renova em 30 dias`). 31 days or more, a next
     charge already past, and any shorter cycle give no mark.
   - `Cobrou após cancelar`, tone `bad`, when the status is `Cancelar` and the latest charge's day is
     after the status day. A charge on the status day or before it gives no mark, and the stored creation
     charge of step 3 never does.

   The stand-in has a fourth mark, `Sobreposta`, between the first two; nothing produces it here, because
   detecting an overlap is later work. `subrules` says which marks hold as values (and the days to a
   renewal); the Portuguese sentences are written in `internal/api/messages.go`, as that file requires.
9. *Charge history.* The charges newest first, the three latest at most (the stand-in's `CHARGES_SHOWN`
   and what the page was designed for), each `{day, amount, foreign}`. With fewer than three, those there
   are. The page keys its rows by day (`SubscriptionCharges.vue`), which one charge per day keeps unique.

**The reads.**
- `subscriptions.list({grouped})` answers `{monthlyTotal, annualTotal, groups, suggestion}`. The monthly
  total is the sum of the monthly equivalents as they are shown (already rounded), over every
  subscription whatever its status; the yearly total is twelve times that monthly total, so the two
  figures of the header agree (six subscriptions of 110.00, 21.90, 13.90, 20.00, 29.90 and 6.67 a month
  give 202.37 and 2428.44). Not grouped: no group at all when there is no subscription, otherwise one
  group with `status: null` holding every subscription in the order they were created (by id), with the
  monthly total. Grouped: one group per status that has any, in the order `Manter`, `Analisar`,
  `Backup e cancelar`, `Cancelar`, each with the sum of its members' monthly equivalents and its members
  in the order they were created. `suggestion` is always null: nothing detects a subscription yet.
- A row is `{id, name, amount, cycle, nextCharge, monthlyEquivalent, line, status, reviewOn,
  reviewOverdue, marks}`. `reviewOverdue` is true when the review day is today or earlier.
- `subscriptions.detail(id)` answers `{id, name, cycle, amount, marks, nextCharge, monthlyEquivalent,
  annualEquivalent, line, status, reviewOn, note, charges, alternatives}` or null. An id is known only
  when it is the plain decimal text of an existing row; `sub-1`, which the recorded cases and the
  interface's sweep over recorded answers use as "nobody has this", stays null. `alternatives` is always
  empty: they are sentences the model writes, and the model is later work.
- `line`, in a row and in the detail, is the name the subscription's line has in the budget in force for
  the current month, or null when the subscription has no line or the current month's budget does not
  have that line. A subscription's line belongs to no month: saving a budget never clears it, and it is
  shown only while the current month's budget has it.
- `subscriptions.recurring` keeps answering `[]`.
- With the snapshot missing every one of these answers `ledger_unavailable`, as today. Without an app's
  database the list has no group, the detail is null and the candidates come from the ledger alone.

**The four setters.** Each names a subscription by id and answers `{changeId}`; the contract's result is
not nullable for any of them.

| method | what it stores | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setStatus(id, status)` | the status, and `status_day` set to today in the same change | the status day moves only when the status really changes |
| `setLine(id, line)` | the id of the line with that name | the name is resolved in the budget of the current month, the built-in fees line under its fixed name included |
| `setReviewDate(id, day)` | the day | a day that is not `YYYY-MM-DD` is `bad_request` |
| `setNote(id, note)` | the note, exactly as sent | |

- A subscription the app's database does not have is refused: `refused` with reason `not_found`. The
  person reads "Esse item não existe mais."
- A line name the current month's budget does not have (a month with no budget included) is refused:
  `refused` with reason `unknown_line`. The person reads "Essa linha não existe no budget desse mês."
- The sentences are the interface's, shown by its central failure function ({{F6}}: the work that teaches
  the interface the `refused` kind and the sentence of each reason); the server sends the reason only.
- A setter that changes nothing (the same status, the same line, the same day, the same note) records an
  empty change and answers its id, whose undo is a no-op.
- The setters read nothing from the ledger and answer the same with the snapshot missing. `create` needs
  the snapshot: without it, it answers `ledger_unavailable` through the same classifier a read uses, and
  records nothing.
- Arguments that do not match the method's schema (a status outside the four, a number where a string
  goes) are `bad_request`, checked by the dispatcher before the handler runs.
- Setting the status is one function of the store, written to be called again: the closing step's "keep"
  and "cancel" of a subscription ({{V3}}: the closing view and its writes) change the status through it,
  under the same rule for the status day.
- Each change is undone with `changes.undo`. An undo that would overwrite something changed since is
  refused with `stale_change` by the recorder: undoing a `create` after a later `setStatus` that is still
  in force is refused, and undoing that `setStatus` first frees it.

**`acceptSuggestion` and `rejectSuggestion`.** They get handlers that answer null and record nothing:
there is no suggestion to act on until something detects one. They leave the `writesWithoutHandler` list
with the other five.

**Failure paths that touch this.**

| what goes wrong | what happens |
| --- | --- |
| the snapshot is missing while `create` runs | `ledger_unavailable`; nothing is recorded |
| a write fails halfway, or waits five seconds for the lock | one transaction: nothing of it is kept; `internal` |
| an undo meets a later change | `stale_change`; nothing is restored |
| the purchase a subscription was made from leaves the ledger, or is excluded | the subscription stays; with no charge left its stored day and amount stand in |
| the bank rewords the establishment so its key changes | the subscription keeps its key and its row; its charges under the old key stay its charges, later purchases under the new key are a new establishment and candidates again; nothing authored is lost |
| a line is renamed | the id holds and the subscription shows the new name |
| a line is removed from the current month's budget | the subscription keeps its `line_id` and shows no line while the month lacks it |
| two tabs create a subscription for one establishment at once | writes queue; the second answers null |
| the process stops between a write's commit and its answer | the change is stored; the interface says the result could not be confirmed and fetches again |

**Where the server departs from the stand-in on purpose.** Each is pinned by a test whose name says what
departs; nothing else may differ.

| departure | stand-in | server |
| --- | --- | --- |
| identity | "already a subscription" is decided by name; the id is `sub-<transaction>` | by establishment key; the id is a minted integer |
| what can be offered | every card debit of the month | movements, fees, unconverted and excluded rows are left out |
| what can be created | only one of the twelve shown | any eligible purchase |
| a new subscription's line | the purchase's line or `'Assinaturas'` | the purchase's line or none; the line is nullable |
| cycle, amount, previous amount, next charge | stored | derived from the charges |
| charge history | invented by stepping back from the next charge | the real charges, one per day |
| `Cobrou após cancelar` | a stored flag | derived from the status day and the latest charge |
| `setLine` | accepts any text | the name must be a line of the current month's budget |
| a setter on an unknown subscription | answers a change that did nothing | refused, `not_found` |
| undo | restores a snapshot of the whole state | by inverse, refused when overwritten since |
| suggestion, recurring purchases, alternatives, `Sobreposta` | seeded | answer nothing |

**Decisions already taken, with what lost.**

| decision | why | what lost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A line named by something that has no month (a subscription) is resolved in the current month | a closed or old month can still be edited, and a line its budget lacks would count nowhere; a subscription has no month of its own | validating everything against the transaction's month; clearing a subscription's line when a budget is saved |
| Unknown targets answer null where the result allows it, and `not_found` where it does not | the screens already treat null as "nothing happened" | refusing every unknown id |
| Ledger rows and authored rows are joined in Go, in one request that sees one snapshot of each store | the reader hands out rows, never a connection, and the snapshot is swapped under it every night | attaching one database to the other; copying the ledger into the app's database |
| The app's database keys a transaction by a key of its own | a pending row is replaced by a posted row under a new provider id | the provider's id as the key |
| Detecting subscriptions is not part of this | it needs thresholds measured on real data | a suggestion and a recurring list invented without a rule |

**Privacy.** The repository is public and a real ledger is a person's whole financial history. Every
fixture here is invented. An establishment key may be a document number: it is never logged and never
printed by a failing test. No proof of this bead needs a real ledger; if one is opened to check a shape,
it is opened read-only, no value from it (amount, description, name, document, id) is printed, logged or
copied into a file, a commit or a pull request, a count may be shown to the person running the test and
goes into no file, and a test that touches it runs only when `FINWISE_LEDGER_SNAPSHOT` names a file. The
golden files' `-update` refuses to run while that variable is set.

**Conventions.** Work in a worktree of your own and end at local commits: atomic, Conventional Commits,
no attribution lines, and no mention of a session, a bead or a plan in a commit message. Money is integer
cents and no float may appear on the money path; the float guard
(`TestNoSourceFileOfTheHTTPLayerTouchesAFloat` in `internal/api/reais_test.go`, as widened since) and the
clock guard must cover `internal/subrules`: if either lists its packages by name, add this one. Every SQL
statement over the app's database is a registered constant in `internal/authored`; `internal/api`
executes none. New files in `internal/api` log nothing. Interface text is Brazilian Portuguese and
everything else is English. A design value in a component comes from a token.

cycle, the next charge, the amount and previous amount, the equivalents, the marks and the history.

its rows' monthly equivalents, and the yearly total is twelve times the monthly total.
- [ ] A subscription whose line the current month's budget does not have, and one with no line, both
answer `"line": null` in the row and in the detail, and the answer validates against the manifest.
- [ ] `subscriptions.detail` of `"sub-1"` still answers `null` in every state, `subscriptions.recurring`

- [ ] The seven names of this bead are gone from `writesWithoutHandler` and the manifest walk passes. On
a server without `--db` the seven still answer `read_only` before their body is read.
- [ ] The contract's two `line` fields are `string | null`; `npm --prefix web run contract` leaves
`internal/contract/contract.json` unchanged once committed; the type check is green.
- [ ] For a subscription with no line: the row's cell reads `Linha do budget=—`; the subtitle under the
name reads the cycle and the equivalent with no third part and no trailing ` · `; the editor's button

- [ ] `npm --prefix web run parity` passes for every state of the subscription screens on both viewports,
and its output is kept for the pull request.
- [ ] `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`
- [ ] Every new test was seen failing once, each against a deliberate break named in the hand-off: the
upper middle gap taken for an even count; same-day rows left as two charges; the next charge computed by
plain month overflow (2027-01-31 becoming 2027-03-03); the "not excluded" condition dropped from the
candidates; the unique constraint removed from the migration; `setStatus` writing the status day
unconditionally; the server answering `'Assinaturas'` for a subscription with no line; the row rendering
`row.line` as it is.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` prints `CI green.`, every worked example above is a passing table test, and a
subscription created from a purchase of the full invented ledger is read back, changed by each of the
four setters and undone to the state before, with `internal/api/testdata/golden/full/` differing from
before in `subscriptions.candidates.json` alone.

## Tests
- Table (unit), `internal/subrules`, invented vectors: the charges (same-day rows, one foreign row, no

  on month ends and leap days, the equivalents and totals ported from the stand-in's vectors in

  equal; a renewal at 0, 1, 30, 31 and minus one day and on a shorter cycle; a charge before, on and
  after the cancelling day), the history's order and its cap of three.
- Property, `internal/subrules`, generated rows: the answer does not depend on the order of the rows; the
  charges' amounts add up to the rows'; the cycle is one of the five; the next charge is after the latest

- Unit, source guards: the package's imports, no float, no `time.Now`, each seen failing.
- Unit, `internal/authored`, a migrated scratch database: the five refusals by the database itself; every
  new statement registered and prepared.
- Golden (read conformance): `full/subscriptions.candidates.json` re-recorded, its diff read; the third

  `subscriptions.detail` (each seeded id and an unknown one) and `subscriptions.candidates` in
  `authoredReadCases`, with their files in `full-authored/`. The invented authored state reaches, over the
  card establishments the full invented ledger has: a subscription on `text:CLOUDSVC SUBSCRIPTION` with
  status `Cancelar` and a status day before 2026-03-10, which shows one foreign charge and the mark
  `Cobrou após cancelar`; one on `text:LIVRARIA EXEMPLO` with a line of the current month's budget when
  the invented state has a budget, and otherwise with a line that budget lacks; one with no line; and one
  on a key no listed transaction has, which shows the stored creation charge.
- Conformance (writes), the harness's modes: a recorded change for `create` and for each setter, with
  its effects' golden file and its undo; nothing to do for the null answers of `create`, for
  `acceptSuggestion` and for `rejectSuggestion`; a refusal case for `not_found` and for `unknown_line`
  (the reason leaves the harness's list of reasons without a producer if it is still there). The strings
  these cases hold that a person would have typed or that name a row (the note, the names, the keys) join
  the list the no-leak test searches the logs for.
- Unit (`httptest`), `internal/api`, ledgers built for the test with `ledgertest`: the candidates' order,
  tie, cap and each exclusion; a subscription with several charge days read through `list` and `detail`;
  the empty change; the stale undo; `bad_request` for a malformed day and status; the reads without an
  app's database. The two existing tests that expect no candidate over the full ledger are rewritten to
  what the rule now says.
- Screen tests (vitest, `createFakeApi` with a seeded state): the row, the narrow subtitle and the editor
  for a subscription with no line, in `assinaturas.test.ts` and `assinatura.test.ts`; unit for
  `rowSubtitle` with and without a line. The existing screen tests and the stand-in's own tests pass
  unchanged.
- Gate: the manifest is current, the type check, the bundle check; parity for the subscription screens.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `internal/subrules/`, `internal/authored/migrations/0006_subscriptions.sql`,
`internal/authored/subscriptions.go`, `internal/authored/authoredtest/`, `internal/api/subscriptions.go`,
`internal/api/subscriptions_writes.go`, `internal/api/subscriptions_test.go`, `internal/api/messages.go`,
`internal/api/testdata/golden/`, `web/src/api/contract/subscriptions.ts`,
`internal/contract/contract.json`, `web/src/api/fake/model.ts`,
`web/src/screens/assinaturas/SubscriptionRow.vue`, `web/src/screens/assinaturas/subscriptionText.ts`,
`web/src/screens/assinaturas/SubscriptionEditor.vue`, `web/src/screens/assinaturas/assinaturas.test.ts`,
`web/src/screens/assinaturas/assinatura.test.ts`
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/fake/subscriptions.ts`, `web/src/api/fake/subscription-rules.ts`,
`web/src/api/fake/subscriptions.test.ts`, `web/src/screens/assinaturas/AssinaturaScreen.vue`,
`web/src/screens/assinaturas/SubscriptionCharges.vue`, `web/src/components/transactions/useLineChange.ts`,
`web/src/test/empty-ledger.test.ts`, `web/src/test/replay-sweep.test.ts`, `web/scripts/parity/states.mjs`,
`internal/txrules/`, `internal/cardrules/calendar.go`, `internal/brday/`, `internal/money/`,
`internal/ledger/`, `internal/api/card.go`, `internal/api/transactions_period.go`,
`internal/api/transactions_wire.go`, `internal/api/reads.go`, `bin/ci`

Four areas: a new package of pure rules; one migration, one store file and the invented state in the
package that owns the app's database; the subscription handlers of the HTTP layer with their golden
files; and, in the interface, one contract file, one type of the stand-in and three components. That is
about fourteen source files, a new table and a contract change, hence `size:L` and the split proposed on
the first line. Three shared files are touched by one entry each and nothing more: the recorder's
registry of journaled tables in `internal/authored` (the `subscriptions` entry), the test file that holds
`writesWithoutHandler` (seven names leave) and, if they list packages by name, the float and clock
guards. `internal/contract/contract.json` is regenerated, never edited. The day and month arithmetic
lives inside `internal/subrules`; `internal/brday` and `internal/cardrules` are not edited. The
transaction handlers, the budget, the review and the stand-in's rules are not touched; the stand-in's
`subscriptions.ts` and `subscription-rules.ts` are the reference being ported and stay as they are.

## Recovery path
The migration adds one table and changes no existing one, and the collector's snapshot is never written,
so nothing of the bank's records can be lost. Before a database that already holds data is migrated, the
runner copies it with `VACUUM INTO` to `<name>.before-<UTC timestamp>` beside it and never overwrites an
existing copy; a migration that fails rolls back its own transaction and `serve` exits naming the path
and the reason. To go back: stop the server; check the copy (`PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok`, the
application id is `0x46494E57`); put it in place of the database with no `-wal` or `-shm` file beside it;
start the binary that goes with it. A binary that does not carry `0006_subscriptions` refuses a database
that records it, instead of guessing, so going back to an older binary means going back to that copy,
and what was typed after the copy was taken is lost with it. A single subscription made by mistake needs
none of this: `changes.undo` of its creation removes it.

title: Add the refused error kind and its closed list of reasons to the contract and the manifest, and hand the argument schemas and the reasons to Go
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing the person sees changes with this piece. Today, when the app cannot do what was asked, the only
things it can say are that it is read-only or that something failed. Once the app starts saving what the
person types it will have to say no for reasons the person can act on: the month is already closed, the
item no longer exists, the change can no longer be undone because something was edited after it. This
piece gives the app and its server one shared, closed vocabulary for those refusals, and gives the
server the exact description of what each action accepts, so that later a malformed request is turned
away before it can touch anything. If it were wrong the person would later read a generic failure where
a reason was due, or a reason that does not match what happened.

## Outcome
The TypeScript contract has an eighth error kind, `refused`, and a closed list of nine reasons, and the
error envelope is a closed union: `refused` always carries exactly one reason of the list, and no other
kind carries one. The manifest is regenerated and says the same. The Go package `internal/contract`
hands out, from the manifest it already embeds, each method's argument schema with the definitions it
refers to, and the list of reasons. No server answers `refused` yet and the interface does nothing new
with it; both come with later slices.

## Context
**The terms.** finwise is a personal finance app for one person, with an interface in `web/` and a Go
backend. *The contract* is the TypeScript interface `FinwiseApi` under `web/src/api/contract/`. *The
manifest* is `internal/contract/contract.json`, generated from the contract by `npm --prefix web run
contract` (`web/scripts/contract-manifest.mjs`), versioned and never edited by hand; `bin/ci` fails when
it is stale (`npm --prefix web run contract:check`). It lists 82 methods: 3 of class `session`, 23
`read`, 1 `evaluate` and 55 `write`, each with a schema for its arguments and one for its result, plus
the schema of the error envelope. *The stand-in* is the in-memory fake backend under `web/src/api/fake/`
that the design prototype runs on; it throws plain errors where the server will answer typed refusals.
Today the backend is read-only: every write and evaluation answers `read_only`. The app is about to gain
its own database, `finwise.db`, and handlers for its writes; this slice is the part of that work that
changes the contract.

**What the code is today (each point checked in the file named).**

- `web/src/api/contract/errors.ts`: `API_ERROR_KINDS` lists `locked`, `read_only`, `ledger_unavailable`,
  `bad_request`, `unknown_method`, `internal` and `network`; `ApiErrorKind` is their union;
  `WireErrorKind` excludes `network`, which only the client raises; `ApiError` is `{ kind }`;
  `ApiErrorEnvelope` is `{ error: { kind: WireErrorKind } }`.
- `web/scripts/contract-manifest.mjs`: walks the methods of `FinwiseApi` with the TypeScript compiler,
  hands each argument type, each result type and `ApiErrorEnvelope` to `ts-json-schema-generator` with
  `additionalProperties: false` and `expose: 'all'`, and writes the manifest with the keys
  `formatVersion`, `description`, `methods`, `error` and `definitions`. Today `error` is
  `{"$ref":"#/definitions/ApiErrorEnvelope"}`.
- The manifest is JSON Schema draft-07. A method's `arguments` is `{"type":"array","items":[...],
  "minItems","maxItems","additionalItems":false}`; an optional parameter is `{"anyOf":[<schema>,
  {"type":"null"}]}`; a `$ref` resolves against the manifest's root as `#/definitions/<Name>`, and some
  names are percent-encoded in the reference (`Exclude%3CApiErrorKind%2C%22network%22%3E`).
- `web/src/api/contract/manifest.test.ts`, "the error envelope": compiles the manifest's `error` schema
  with Ajv and expects `{error:{kind}}` to be valid for every wire kind, and `{error:{kind:"network"}}`,
  an envelope with an extra field and a bare `{kind}` to be invalid.
- `internal/contract/contract.go`: `Load` parses the embedded manifest into `[]Method`, each with
  `Domain`, `Name`, `Route`, `Class`, `MinArguments` and `MaxArguments`, and fails on anything it does
  not understand (an unknown class, a wrong route, a duplicate). `manifestFile` reads only `methods`,
  and `argumentsSchema` keeps `items` only to count them: the argument schemas, the `definitions` and
  the `error` schema are not exposed. `internal/api/router.go` therefore checks only how many arguments
  arrived.
- `internal/api/conformance_test.go` already compiles every method's result schema with
  `github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` (a direct requirement in `go.mod`), draft 7, by reading the
  manifest file from disk and placing each schema in a document that carries the `definitions`. No
  non-test file imports that library.
- `web/src/api/http/client.ts`: `failureKind` accepts any kind of `API_ERROR_KINDS` except `network` and
  turns anything else into `internal`. `web/src/api/failures.ts` handles `read_only`, `locked` and
  `ledger_unavailable` by name and shows "Não foi possível carregar os dados." with "Tentar de novo" for
  every other kind.

**1. The `refused` kind.** The envelope becomes a closed union: every kind but `refused` has no other
field; `refused` always carries one reason of a closed list.

```
{"error": {"kind": "refused", "reason": "<one of the list>"}}      HTTP 409
```

| reason | when | what the person reads (the interface's text; the server sends none) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `month_closed` | saving or applying a budget for a closed month; closing a month already closed | "Esse mês já está fechado." |
| `future_month` | closing a month after the current one | "Esse mês ainda não chegou." |
| `pending_reviews` | closing a month while a transaction of that month or an earlier one waits for review | "Resolva as pendências do mês antes de fechar." |
| `stale_change` | undoing or extending a change that is unknown, already undone, already extended, or overwritten since | "Isso já foi alterado depois e não pode mais ser desfeito." |
| `not_found` | a write whose result cannot be null names a transaction, pot, subscription or establishment that the ledger does not list or `finwise.db` does not have | "Esse item não existe mais." |
| `unknown_line` | a write names a budget line that the budget of the month it is resolved in does not have | "Essa linha não existe no budget desse mês." |
| `invalid_budget` | saving a budget with a duplicate or empty line name, an unknown or repeated line id, an unknown group | "O budget tem linha sem nome ou repetida." |
| `unstable_pot` | a write to a pot whose identity the bank does not keep stable | "O banco não identifica esse cofrinho de forma estável." |
| `split_with_reimbursement` | splitting a purchase that has a linked reimbursement, or linking one to a split purchase | "Uma compra dividida não pode ter reembolso ligado." |

In `errors.ts`, `refused` joins the kinds, the nine reasons are a closed list written in the style of
`API_ERROR_KINDS` (a constant array and the union derived from it, in the order of the table), and
`ApiErrorEnvelope` is the union. How the type is spelled so that the generator emits a closed union is
the implementer's; `contract-manifest.mjs` is edited only if the generator cannot express it from the
type. The sentences are not this slice's and are written nowhere here: the texts stay in the interface
and are wired by the slice that teaches the interface this kind ({{F6}}: the reason and the method's
class on a failure, the sentence of each reason, and what a failed write does on screen). The other
kinds keep their meaning: `bad_request` is for arguments that do not match the method's schema or cannot
be parsed, which is a bug in a client, and `read_only` stays for a server without its own database and
for a write that has no handler yet.

Until the interface is taught, adding the kind changes nothing a person can meet: no server answers
`refused` before the write dispatch exists ({{F4c}}: the router running handlers for writes, the
`refused` answer in Go and the first write, undo), and if one did, the HTTP client would pass `refused`
through as a kind with no reason and `failures.ts` would show its default wording. This slice edits
neither `client.ts` nor `failures.ts`, and the stand-in does not change: it has no envelope.

**2. `internal/contract` hands out the argument schemas and the reasons.** The package learns to hand
out, from the manifest it already embeds: for each method, its argument schema together with the
definitions it refers to, in a form the schema library can compile (the write dispatch compiles them
when the server starts and applies them before a write's handler runs); and the list of reasons, in the
manifest's order, so that the Go side of the refusal can be held equal to the contract by a test. `Load`
keeps failing on what it does not understand: a method with no argument schema, or a manifest in which
